title.zh: 卷一百六十四 列傳第五十一: 楊恭懿 王恂 郭守敬 楊桓 楊果 王構 魏初 焦養直 孟攀麟 尚野 李之紹
title.en: Volume 164 Biographies 51: Yang Gongyi, Wang Xun, Guo Shoujing, Yang Huan, Yang Guo, Wang Gou, Wei Chu, Jiao Yangzhi, Meng Panlin, Shang Ye, Li Zhishao
title.raw: 卷一百六十四 列傳第五十一: 楊恭懿 王恂 郭守敬 楊桓 楊果 王構 魏初 焦養直 孟攀麟 尚野 李之紹 Volume 164 Biographies 51: Yang Gongyi, Wang Xun, Guo Shoujing, Yang Huan, Yang Guo, Wang Gou, Wei Chu, Jiao Yangzhi, Meng Panlin, Shang Ye, Li Zhishao

sentences.zh: 楊恭懿

translations.literal: Yang Gongyi
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongyi

sentences.zh: 楊恭懿，字元甫，奉元人。

translations.literal: Yang Gongyi, styled Yuanfu, was a native of Fengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongyi, courtesy name Yuanfu, came from Fengyuan.

sentences.zh: 力學強記，日數千言，雖從親逃亂，未嘗廢業。

translations.literal: He studied with vigor and had a powerful memory, reciting several thousand characters a day; though he fled turmoil with his kin, he never abandoned his studies.
translations.idiomatic: He applied himself to learning and had an exceptional memory, memorizing several thousand characters a day; even while fleeing chaos with his family, he never neglected his studies.

sentences.zh: 年十七，西還，家貧，服勞為養。

translations.literal: At seventeen he returned west; his family was poor, and he performed manual labor to support them.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of seventeen he returned to the west. The family was poor, and he took on physical labor to provide for them.

sentences.zh: 暇則就學，書無不讀，尤深於《易》、《禮》、《春秋》，後得硃熹集注《四書》，歎曰：「人倫日用之常，天道性命之妙，皆萃此書矣。」

translations.literal: In his spare time he pursued learning and read every book; he was especially deep in the Changes, Rites, and Spring and Autumn Annals. Later he obtained Zhu Xi's collected commentaries on the Four Books and sighed, saying: "The constants of human relations in daily life and the subtleties of the Way of Heaven and human nature are all gathered in this book."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he had leisure he studied. There was no book he did not read, and he was especially versed in the Book of Changes, the Book of Rites, and the Spring and Autumn Annals. Later he obtained Zhu Xi's collected commentaries on the Four Books and exclaimed: "The norms of human conduct in everyday life and the mysteries of the Way of Heaven and human nature are all concentrated in this work."

sentences.zh: 父沒，水漿不入口者五日，居喪盡禮。

translations.literal: When his father died, for five days he would not take water or gruel, and in mourning he fulfilled every rite.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he took neither water nor gruel for five days, and throughout the mourning period he observed the rites in full.

sentences.zh: 宣撫司、行省以掌書記辟，不就。

translations.literal: The Pacification Commission and the Branch Secretariat invited him as chief secretary, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification Commission and the Branch Secretariat both offered him the post of chief secretary, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 至元七年，與許衡俱被召，恭懿不至。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan, he and Xu Heng were both summoned; Gongyi did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Zhiyuan era (1270), he and Xu Heng were both summoned to court, but Gongyi did not go.

sentences.zh: 衡拜中書左丞，日於右相安童前稱譽恭懿之賢，丞相以聞。

translations.literal: Heng was appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and daily before the Right Chancellor Antong praised Gongyi's worth; the chancellor reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and each day before the Right Chancellor Antong spoke of Gongyi's excellence; the chancellor reported this to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 十年，詔遣使召之，以疾不起。

translations.literal: In the tenth year an edict sent envoys to summon him; he pleaded illness and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1273) an edict dispatched envoys to summon him; citing illness, he did not go.

sentences.zh: 十一年，太子下教中書，俾如漢惠聘四皓者以聘恭懿，丞相遣郎中張元智為書致命，乃至京師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Crown Prince issued instructions to the Secretariat that Gongyi should be invited as Emperor Hui of Han had invited the Four Hoary Ones; the chancellor sent Gentleman-of-the-Interior Zhang Yuanzhi with a letter conveying the command, and only then did he reach the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Crown Prince instructed the Secretariat to invite Gongyi as Emperor Hui of Han had invited the Four Hoary Ones of Mount Shang; the chancellor sent Gentleman-of-the-Interior Zhang Yuanzhi with a letter bearing the imperial command, and only then did he arrive at the capital.

sentences.zh: 既入見，世祖遣國王和童勞其遠來，繼又親詢其鄉里、族氏、師承、子姓，無不周悉。

translations.literal: After he had been received in audience, Kublai sent Prince Hetong to console him for his long journey; afterward the emperor personally inquired into his native place, clan, teachers, and children and grandchildren, leaving nothing unasked.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had been received in audience, Kublai sent Prince Hetong to welcome him for his long journey. The emperor then personally questioned him about his native district, clan, teachers, and descendants, omitting nothing.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月二日，帝御香殿，以大軍南征，使久不至，命筮之，其言秘。

translations.literal: On the second day of the first month of the twelfth year, the emperor attended the Incense Hall. Because the great army on the southern campaign had long failed to return, he ordered divination performed; the oracle's words were kept secret.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the first month of the twelfth year, the emperor took his seat in the Incense Hall. Because the main force on the southern campaign had long failed to return, he ordered divination; the pronouncement was kept secret.

sentences.zh: 侍讀學士徒單公履請設取士科，詔與恭懿議之。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Tutuha Gonglu requested the establishment of a civil service examination; an edict ordered discussion with Gongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Tutuha Gonglu requested that a civil examination be established; an edict ordered that this be discussed with Gongyi.

sentences.zh: 恭懿言：「明詔有謂：士不治經學孔孟之道，日為賦詩空文。

translations.literal: Gongyi said: "A clear edict states that scholars who do not cultivate the classics and the Way of Confucius and Mencius daily compose fu and empty literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi said: "A clear edict declares that when scholars do not pursue the classics and the Way of Confucius and Mencius, they spend their days writing fu and hollow literary compositions.

sentences.zh: 斯言誠萬世治安之本。

translations.literal: These words are truly the foundation of peace and order for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: This statement is indeed the foundation of enduring peace and good government.

sentences.zh: 今欲取士，宜敕有司，舉有行檢、通經史之士，使無投牒自售，試以經義、論策。

translations.literal: Now, if men are to be selected, the responsible offices should be ordered to recommend men of good conduct who are versed in the classics and histories, so that none may present memorials to sell themselves, and they should be tested on the meaning of the classics and policy essays.
translations.idiomatic: If scholars are now to be selected, the responsible offices should be instructed to recommend men of proven character who are versed in the classics and histories, so that none may submit petitions to peddle themselves, and they should be examined on classical interpretation and policy essays.

sentences.zh: 夫既從事實學，則士風還淳，民俗趨厚，國家得才矣。」

translations.literal: Once they engage in solid learning, scholarly custom will return to simplicity, popular custom will tend toward thickness, and the state will obtain talent.
translations.idiomatic: Once scholars devote themselves to substantive learning, the tone of the literati will return to purity, the people's ways will grow more substantial, and the state will gain able men.

sentences.zh: 奏之，帝善之。

translations.literal: He memorialized this; the emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted this memorial, and the emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 會北征，恭懿遂歸田裡。

translations.literal: When the northern campaign was launched, Gongyi returned to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern campaign began, Gongyi returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 十六年，詔安西王相敦遣赴闕。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year an edict ordered the Anxi King's chancellor Dun to send him to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year an edict instructed the Anxi King's chancellor Dun to escort him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 入見，詔於太史院改歷。

translations.literal: After audience he was ordered to reform the calendar at the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: After he was received in audience, an edict assigned him to the Directorate of Astronomy to reform the calendar.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月，進奏曰：「臣等遍考自漢以來曆書四十餘家，精思推算，舊儀難用，而新者未備，故日行盈縮，月行遲疾，五行周天，其詳皆未精察。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventeenth year he submitted a memorial saying: "We have comprehensively examined more than forty calendrical works since Han times and pondered their calculations with care. The old instruments are hard to use, and the new ones are not yet complete; thus the sun's advance and retreat, the moon's swift and slow motion, and the five planets' circuit of heaven have none been examined with precision in detail.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventeenth year he presented a memorial stating: "We have surveyed more than forty calendrical treatises from Han times onward and deliberated on their calculations. The old instruments are difficult to apply, and newer methods remain incomplete; accordingly, the sun's varying pace, the moon's alternating speed, and the five planets' circuits have none been scrutinized with sufficient precision.

sentences.zh: 今權以新儀木表，與舊儀所測相較，得今歲冬至晷景及日躔所在，與列舍分度之差，大都北極之高下，晝夜刻長短，參以古制，創立新法，推算成《辛巳曆》。

translations.literal: For the present we provisionally use the new wooden gnomon instrument and compare it with measurements by the old instrument, obtaining this year's winter solstice shadow length and the sun's position, the difference in lodge degrees, the height of the pole star at Dadu, and the lengths of day and night in quarter-hours; consulting ancient regulations, we have created a new method and calculated the Xinsi Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: For now we have provisionally employed the new wooden gnomon and compared its readings with those of the old instrument, determining this year's winter-solstice shadow, the sun's position, discrepancies in lodge divisions, the altitude of the pole star at Dadu, and the lengths of day and night in quarter-hours. Drawing on ancient models, we have devised a new method and completed calculations for the Xinsi Calendar.

sentences.zh: 雖或未精，然比之前改歷者，附會曆元，更立日法，全踵故習，顧亦無愧。

translations.literal: Though it may not yet be precise, compared with previous calendar reformers who forced the epoch to fit, established new day-fraction methods, and wholly followed old habits, we may still be without shame.
translations.idiomatic: Although it may not yet be fully precise, compared with earlier calendar reformers who forced the epoch to conform, devised new day-fraction rules, and merely followed old conventions, we have nothing to be ashamed of.

sentences.zh: 然必每歲測驗修改，積三十年，庶盡其法。

translations.literal: Yet it must be tested and revised every year; accumulated over thirty years, one may hope to exhaust its method.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the calendar must be tested and revised annually; only after thirty years of accumulation might its method be fully perfected.

sentences.zh: 可使如三代日官，世專其職，測驗良久，無改歲之事矣。」

translations.literal: One may then have officers like the day-officers of the Three Dynasties, who generation after generation hold their office, test for a long time, and have no need to change the year-establishment."
translations.idiomatic: Then officers like the calendrical specialists of the Three Dynasties could hold the post hereditarily, observe over long periods, and there would be no further need to reform the calendar."

sentences.zh: 又《合朔議》曰：

translations.literal: He also presented a "Discussion on Conjunction and New Moon," saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a "Memorial on Conjunction and New Moon," which stated:

sentences.zh: 日行歷四時一周，謂之一歲；

translations.literal: The sun's course passing through the four seasons once around is called one year;
translations.idiomatic: When the sun completes one circuit through the four seasons, that is called a year;

sentences.zh: 月逾一周，復與日合，謂之一月；

translations.literal: the moon passing beyond one circuit and again joining the sun is called one month;
translations.idiomatic: when the moon completes a circuit and again joins the sun, that is called a month;

sentences.zh: 言一月之始，日月相合，故謂合朔。

translations.literal: That is to say, at the beginning of a month sun and moon join, hence it is called conjunction and new moon.
translations.idiomatic: This means that at the start of a month the sun and moon conjoin, which is why it is termed conjunction and new moon.

sentences.zh: 自秦廢歷紀，漢太初止用平朔法，大小相間，或有二大者，故日食多在晦日或二日，測驗時刻亦鮮中。

translations.literal: Since Qin abolished the calendar chronology, Han Taichu used only the mean-conjunction method, large and small months alternating, sometimes with two large months; thus solar eclipses mostly fell on the last day or the second day, and tested moments rarely hit center.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin abolished calendrical chronology, the Han Taichu calendar relied solely on mean conjunctions, alternating long and short months and sometimes producing two long months in succession; solar eclipses therefore often fell on the last day of the month or the second day, and observed times rarely matched predictions.

sentences.zh: 宋何承天測驗四十餘年，進《元嘉曆》，始以月行遲速定小餘以正朔望，使食必在朔，名定朔法，有三大二小，時以異舊法罷之。

translations.literal: Song He Chengtian tested for more than forty years and presented the Yuanjia Calendar, first using the moon's swift and slow motion to fix the small remainder and correct new and full moons, so that eclipses must fall on new moon—called the true-conjunction method, with three large and two small months; at the time it was rejected as differing from the old method.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian of Song observed for more than forty years and submitted the Yuanjia Calendar, first employing the moon's varying speed to adjust the fractional remainder and correct new and full moons so that eclipses would invariably fall on the new moon—a method called true conjunction, producing three long and two short months in sequence; contemporaries rejected it as departing from established practice.

sentences.zh: 梁虞廣刂造《大同曆》，隋劉焯造《皇極曆》，皆用定朔，為時所阻。

translations.literal: Liang Yu Guang created the Datong Calendar, Sui Liu Chuo created the Huangji Calendar—both used true conjunction and were blocked by their times.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Guang of Liang devised the Datong Calendar, and Liu Chuo of Sui the Huangji Calendar; both employed true conjunction but were obstructed by their contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 唐傅仁均造《戊寅曆》，定朔始得行。

translations.literal: Tang Fu Renjun created the Wuyin Calendar, and true conjunction first came into use.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Renjun of Tang created the Wuyin Calendar, and true conjunction was first put into practice.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十九年，四月頻大，人皆異之，竟改從平朔。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhenguan, the fourth month was frequently large; all regarded it as strange, and in the end they reverted to mean conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of the Zhenguan reign, several consecutive long fourth months astonished everyone, and the calendar was ultimately reverted to mean conjunction.

sentences.zh: 李淳風造《麟德曆》，雖不用平朔，遇四大則避人言，以平朔間之，又希合當世，為進朔法，使無元日之食。

translations.literal: Li Chunfeng created the Linde Calendar; though he did not use mean conjunction, when there were four large months he avoided popular talk by inserting mean conjunction between them; he also hoped to suit the age and devised the advancing-new-moon method so there would be no eclipse on New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chunfeng devised the Linde Calendar; although he did not employ mean conjunction, whenever four long months occurred he appeased public opinion by interposing mean conjunctions. He also sought to accommodate contemporary expectations with an advancing-new-moon method designed to prevent eclipses on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 至一行造《大衍曆》，謂「天事誠密，四大三小何傷。」

translations.literal: When Yixing created the Dayan Calendar, he said: "Heaven's affairs are truly subtle; what harm is there in four large and three small months?"
translations.idiomatic: When the monk Yixing devised the Dayan Calendar, he declared: "Heaven's operations are truly precise; what injury is there in four long and three short months?"

sentences.zh: 誠為確論，然亦循常不改。

translations.literal: This was indeed a sound judgment, yet they still followed convention without change.
translations.idiomatic: This was indeed sound doctrine, yet calendrists continued to follow convention without reform.

sentences.zh: 臣等更造新歷，一依前賢定論，推算皆改從實。

translations.literal: We have further created a new calendar, wholly following the settled judgments of former worthies; all calculations are changed to follow reality.
translations.idiomatic: We have now devised a new calendar, adhering entirely to the settled conclusions of earlier masters; all calculations have been revised to conform to actual observation.

sentences.zh: 今十九年曆，自八月後，四月並大，實日月合朔之數也。

translations.literal: In the calendar for the nineteenth year, from the eighth month onward four months are all large—this is truly the number of sun-and-moon conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: In the calendar for the nineteenth year, from the eighth month onward four consecutive long months appear—this reflects the actual count of solar-lunar conjunction.

sentences.zh: 詳見《郭守敬傳》。

translations.literal: For details see the biography of Guo Shoujing.
translations.idiomatic: For further particulars see the biography of Guo Shoujing.

sentences.zh: 是日，方列跪，未讀奏，帝命許衡及恭懿起，曰：「卿二老，毋自勞也。」

translations.literal: That day, as they were kneeling in rank and before the memorial was read, the emperor ordered Xu Heng and Gongyi to rise, saying: "You two elders, do not weary yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: That day, as they knelt in formation before the memorial could be read, the emperor directed Xu Heng and Gongyi to rise, saying: "You two venerable gentlemen, spare yourselves the strain."

sentences.zh: 授集賢​​學士，兼太史院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies and concurrently charged with affairs of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies and concurrently placed in charge of the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 十八年，辭歸。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 二十年，以太子賓客召；

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was summoned as Mentor to the Heir Apparent;
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was summoned as Mentor to the Heir Apparent;

sentences.zh: 二十二年，以昭文館學士、領太史院事召；

translations.literal: in the twenty-second year he was summoned as Academician of the Zhaowen Hall and director of the Directorate of Astronomy;
translations.idiomatic: in the twenty-second year he was summoned as Academician of the Zhaowen Hall to head the Directorate of Astronomy;

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以議中書省事召。

translations.literal: in the twenty-ninth year he was summoned to deliberate on Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: in the twenty-ninth year he was summoned to deliberate on Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 皆不行。

translations.literal: He accepted none of these.
translations.idiomatic: He declined every summons.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，卒，年七十。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: ○王恂

translations.literal: ○ Wang Xun
translations.idiomatic: ○ Wang Xun

sentences.zh: 王恂，字敬甫，中山唐縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Xun, styled Jingfu, was a native of Tang County in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun, courtesy name Jingfu, came from Tang County in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 父良，金末為中山府掾，時民遭亂後，多以詿誤繫獄，良前後所活數百人。

translations.literal: His father Liang, at the end of Jin served as clerk of Zhongshan Prefecture; at that time after the people had suffered turmoil, many were imprisoned on false charges, and Liang before and after saved several hundred lives.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liang served as a clerk in Zhongshan Prefecture at the end of the Jin dynasty. After the chaos, many people were imprisoned on trumped-up charges; Liang saved several hundred lives in all.

sentences.zh: 已而棄去吏業，潛心伊洛之學，及天文律曆，無不精究，年九十二卒。

translations.literal: Later he abandoned official service and devoted himself to the learning of the Cheng brothers of Luoyang, as well as astronomy, pitch-pipes, and calendrics, mastering all without exception; he died at ninety-two.
translations.idiomatic: He later abandoned official life and devoted himself to the Neo-Confucian learning of the Cheng brothers, as well as astronomy, harmonics, and calendrics, mastering all of these fields. He died at ninety-two.

sentences.zh: 恂性穎悟，生三歲，家人示以書帙，輒識風、丁二字。

translations.literal: Xun was by nature quick-witted; at three years old, when his family showed him books, he at once recognized the characters feng and ding.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was exceptionally bright. At the age of three, when his family showed him books, he immediately recognized the characters for "wind" and "fourth."

sentences.zh: 母劉氏，授以《千字文》，再過目，即成誦。

translations.literal: His mother, née Liu, taught him the Thousand-Character Classic; after two readings he could recite it from memory.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Liu, taught him the Thousand-Character Classic; after reading it twice he could recite it from memory.

sentences.zh: 六歲就學，十三學九數，輒造其極。

translations.literal: At six he began formal study; at thirteen he studied the nine branches of mathematics and at once reached their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: At six he entered formal schooling; at thirteen he studied the nine branches of mathematics and immediately attained mastery.

sentences.zh: 歲己酉，太保劉秉忠北上，途經中山，見而奇之，及南還，從秉忠學於磁之紫金山。

translations.literal: In the year jiyou, Grand Guardian Liu Bingzhong went north and passed through Zhongshan; seeing him he marveled at him, and when he returned south Xun followed Bingzhong to study at Purple Gold Mountain in Ci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiyou year Grand Guardian Liu Bingzhong traveled north and passed through Zhongshan; struck by the boy's talent, he took him south on his return to study at Purple Gold Mountain in Ci Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，秉忠薦之世祖，召見於六盤山，命輔導裕宗，為太子伴讀。

translations.literal: In guichou, Bingzhong recommended him to Kublai; he was summoned to audience at Liupan Mountain and ordered to instruct Prince Yuzong as companion reader to the heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the guichou year Bingzhong recommended him to Kublai. He was received in audience at Liupan Mountain and appointed to guide Prince Yuzong as companion reader to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，擢太子贊善，時年二十八。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong he was promoted to Supporter of Goodness to the Heir Apparent, aged twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhongtong era he was promoted to Supporter of Goodness to the Heir Apparent at the age of twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 三年，裕宗封燕王，守中書令，兼判樞密院事，敕兩府大臣：凡有諮禀，必令王恂與聞。

translations.literal: In the third year Prince Yuzong was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan, held the post of Director of the Secretariat, and concurrently judged Military Affairs Commission affairs; an edict to ministers of both offices said: whatever consultations and reports there are, Wang Xun must be informed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Prince Yuzong was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan, served as Director of the Secretariat, and concurrently oversaw the Military Affairs Commission. An edict instructed ministers of both offices that Wang Xun must be informed of every consultation and report.

sentences.zh: 初，中書左丞許衡集唐、虞以來嘉言善政，為書以進。

translations.literal: Earlier, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Xu Heng collected fine words and good policies from Tang and Yu onward and made a book to present.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Left Vice Director Xu Heng had compiled a book of exemplary sayings and sound policies from the age of Yao and Shun onward and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗令恂講解，且命太子受業焉。

translations.literal: Kublai once ordered Xun to expound it and also commanded the heir to receive instruction from him.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai once directed Xun to expound the work and ordered the heir apparent to study under him.

sentences.zh: 又詔恂於太子起居飲食，慎為調護，非所宜接之人，勿令得侍左右。

translations.literal: He also ordered Xun carefully to regulate the heir's daily life, food, and drink, and not to let unsuitable persons attend at his side.
translations.idiomatic: He further instructed Xun to supervise the heir's daily routine, diet, and conduct with care, and not to allow unsuitable persons to wait upon him.

sentences.zh: 恂言：「太子天下本，付託至重，當延名德與之居處。

translations.literal: Xun said: "The heir is the root of the empire; the charge entrusted is extremely heavy. One should invite men of renowned virtue to dwell with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun said: "The heir apparent is the foundation of the realm; the trust placed in him is weighty in the extreme. Men of eminent virtue should be invited to keep his company.

sentences.zh: 況兼領中書、樞密之政，詔條所當遍覽，庶務亦當屢省，官吏以罪免者毋使更進，軍官害人，改用之際，尤不可非其人。

translations.literal: Moreover, since he concurrently holds Secretariat and Military Affairs affairs, edicts and regulations should be read through in full, and routine matters should also be frequently reviewed; officials dismissed for crimes must not be allowed to advance again; when military officers harm the people and are replaced, above all the wrong men must not be appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since he concurrently oversees Secretariat and Military Affairs affairs, he should read through all edicts and regulations and frequently review routine business. Officials dismissed for misconduct must not be reappointed. When military officers harm the people and are replaced, particular care must be taken not to appoint unworthy successors.

sentences.zh: 民至愚而神，變亂之餘，吾不之疑，則反覆化為忠厚。」

translations.literal: The people are most foolish yet divine; after the changes of turmoil, if we do not suspect them, they will in turn be transformed into honesty and generosity.
translations.idiomatic: The people are profoundly simple yet responsive; after the upheavals of disorder, if we do not distrust them, they will in time be transformed into honest and steadfast subjects.

sentences.zh: 帝深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly approved these words.

sentences.zh: 恂早以算術名，裕宗嘗問焉。

translations.literal: Xun early gained fame for mathematics; Prince Yuzong once questioned him about it.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had early won renown for mathematics, and Prince Yuzong once questioned him on the subject.

sentences.zh: 恂曰：「算數，六藝之一，定國家，安人民，乃大事也。」

translations.literal: Xun said: "Mathematics is one of the Six Arts; to settle the state and secure the people is a great matter."
translations.idiomatic: Xun replied: "Mathematics is one of the Six Arts. To establish the state and secure the people is a matter of the greatest importance."

sentences.zh: 每侍左右，必發明三綱五常，為學之道，及歷代治忽興亡之所以然。

translations.literal: Whenever he attended at the prince's side, he always expounded the Three Bonds and Five Constants, the Way of learning, and the reasons for the rise and fall, order and disorder of successive dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he attended the prince, he expounded the Three Bonds and Five Constants, the principles of learning, and the causes behind the rise and fall of successive dynasties.

sentences.zh: 又以遼、金之事近接耳目者，區別其善惡，論著其得失，上之。

translations.literal: He also took events of Liao and Jin that were close at hand to the senses, distinguished their good and evil, discussed their gains and losses, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He also drew on recent events of the Liao and Jin dynasties still fresh in memory, distinguished their virtues and faults, analyzed their successes and failures, and submitted his findings.

sentences.zh: 裕宗問以心之所守，恂曰：「許衡嘗言：人心如印板，惟板本不差，則雖摹千萬紙皆不差；

translations.literal: Prince Yuzong asked what the heart should hold fast to; Xun said: "Xu Heng once said: The human heart is like a printing block—only if the block itself is not wrong will even ten thousand impressions on paper be without error;
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yuzong asked what the heart should hold fast to, Xun said: "Xu Heng once remarked that the human heart is like a printing block: only if the block itself is true will every impression, even ten thousand sheets, be without flaw;

sentences.zh: 本既差，則摹之於紙，無不差者。」

translations.literal: if the root is already wrong, then whatever is impressed on paper will be without exception wrong."
translations.idiomatic: but if the block is flawed, every impression on paper will be flawed without exception."

sentences.zh: 裕宗深然之。

translations.literal: Prince Yuzong deeply approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuzong strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔擇勳戚子弟，使學於恂，師道卓然。

translations.literal: An edict selected sons and younger brothers of meritorious kin to study under Xun; his teaching authority stood eminent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict selected sons of meritorious families to study under Xun, whose authority as teacher stood eminent.

sentences.zh: 及恂從裕宗撫軍稱海，乃以諸生屬之許衡，及衡告老而去，復命恂領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When Xun followed Prince Yuzong in pacifying the army at Chenghai, the students were entrusted to Xu Heng; when Heng requested retirement and left, Xun was again ordered to head the Directorate of Education as libationer.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun accompanied Prince Yuzong in pacifying the army at Chenghai, the students were placed under Xu Heng's charge. After Heng retired, Xun was again appointed libationer of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 國學之制，實始於此。

translations.literal: The institution of the National University in fact began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The institution of the National University in fact dates from this period.

sentences.zh: 帝以國朝承用金《大明曆》，歲久浸疏，欲厘正之，知恂精於算術，遂以命之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the dynasty had inherited the Jin Great Enlightenment Calendar and over the years it had grown increasingly loose, wished to rectify it; knowing Xun was expert in mathematics, he thereupon charged him with it.
translations.idiomatic: Because the dynasty had inherited the Jin Great Enlightenment Calendar, which had grown increasingly inaccurate over the years, the emperor wished to reform it. Knowing Xun's mastery of mathematics, he entrusted him with the task.

sentences.zh: 恂薦許衡能明歷之理，詔驛召赴闕，命領改歷事，官屬悉聽恂辟置。

translations.literal: Xun recommended Xu Heng as able to clarify calendrical principles; an edict summoned him by post-horse to court and ordered him to head calendar reform; all subordinates were to be appointed at Xun's selection.
translations.idiomatic: Xun recommended Xu Heng as one who understood calendrical principles. An edict summoned him by relay to court and placed him in charge of calendar reform; all staff were to be appointed at Xun's discretion.

sentences.zh: 恂與衡及楊恭懿、郭守敬等，遍考曆書四十餘家，晝夜測驗，創立新法，參以古制，推算極為精密，詳在《守敬傳》。

translations.literal: Xun with Heng and Yang Gongyi, Guo Shoujing, and others comprehensively examined more than forty calendrical works, tested day and night, created a new method, consulted ancient regulations, and calculated with extreme precision; details are in the biography of Shoujing.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, together with Heng, Yang Gongyi, Guo Shoujing, and others, surveyed more than forty calendrical treatises and observed day and night. They devised a new method, drew on ancient models, and achieved calculations of exceptional precision; particulars appear in the biography of Guo Shoujing.

sentences.zh: 十六年，授嘉議大夫、太史令。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Grand Master of Court Discussion and Director of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Grand Master of Court Discussion and Director of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 十七年，歷成，賜名《授時曆》，以其年冬頒行天下。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the calendar was completed and given the name Season-Granting Calendar; that winter it was promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the calendar was completed and named the Season-Granting Calendar; that winter it was promulgated throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 十八年，居父喪，哀毀，日飲勺水。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, while in mourning for his father, he was grief-stricken and wasted away, drinking only a spoonful of water a day.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, while mourning his father, he was consumed by grief and took only a spoonful of water each day.

sentences.zh: 帝遣內侍慰諭之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace attendant to console and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace attendant to console him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 初，恂病，裕宗屢遣醫診治，及葬，賻鈔二千貫。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xun was ill, Prince Yuzong repeatedly sent physicians to treat him; at his burial he was given two thousand strings of paper money as funeral gift.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun fell ill, Prince Yuzong repeatedly sent physicians to treat him. At his burial the prince granted two thousand strings of paper money as funeral compensation.

sentences.zh: 後帝思定歷之功，以鈔五千貫賜其家。

translations.literal: Later the emperor, recalling his merit in fixing the calendar, bestowed five thousand strings of paper money on his family.
translations.idiomatic: Later, recalling his service in establishing the calendar, the emperor granted his family five thousand strings of paper money.

sentences.zh: 延祐二年，贈推忠守正功臣、光祿大夫、司徒、上柱國、定國公，諡文肅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanyou he was posthumously given the title Meritorious Subject Who Pushes Loyalty and Upholds Rectitude, Grand Master of the Imperial Household, Minister of Education, Pillar of the State of the First Rank, and Duke Who Settles the State, with posthumous name Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yanyou era he was posthumously honored as Meritorious Subject Who Pushes Loyalty and Upholds Rectitude, Grand Master of the Imperial Household, Minister of Education, Pillar of the State of the First Rank, and Duke Who Settles the State, with the posthumous name Wensu.

sentences.zh: 子寬、賓，並從許衡遊，得星曆之傳於家學。

translations.literal: His sons Kuan and Bin both studied under Xu Heng and received the transmission of astronomy and calendrics from family learning.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Kuan and Bin both studied under Xu Heng and inherited the family's expertise in astronomy and calendrics.

sentences.zh: 裕宗嘗召見，語之曰：「汝父起於書生，貧無貲蓄，今賜汝鈔五千貫，用盡可復以聞。」

translations.literal: Prince Yuzong once summoned them to audience and said to them: "Your father rose from a scholar's family and was poor without savings; now I bestow on you five thousand strings of paper money—when it is used up you may report again."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuzong once summoned them and said: "Your father rose from scholarly poverty without savings. I now grant you five thousand strings of paper money; when it is spent, you may request more."

sentences.zh: 恩卹之厚如此。

translations.literal: Favor and condolence were this generous.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of the favor shown them.

sentences.zh: 寬由保章正歷兵部郎中，知蠡州。

translations.literal: Kuan rose from Director of the Astrological Bureau through Libationer of the Calendar to Gentleman-of-the-Interior in the Ministry of War and served as prefect of Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan rose from Director of the Astrological Bureau through Libationer of the Calendar to Gentleman-of-the-Interior in the Ministry of War and served as prefect of Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 賓由保章副累遷秘書監。

translations.literal: Bin rose from Vice Director of the Astrological Bureau through successive promotions to Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Bin rose from Vice Director of the Astrological Bureau through successive promotions to Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: ○郭守敬

translations.literal: ○ Guo Shoujing
translations.idiomatic: ○ Guo Shoujing

sentences.zh: 郭守敬，字若思，順德邢台人。

translations.literal: Guo Shoujing, styled Ruosi, was a native of Xingtai in Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shoujing, courtesy name Ruosi, came from Xingtai in Shunde.

sentences.zh: 生有異操，不為嬉戲事。

translations.literal: From birth he had an unusual disposition and did not engage in playful matters.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he showed an unusual temperament and never engaged in frivolous pastimes.

sentences.zh: 大父榮，通五經，精於算數、水利。

translations.literal: His grandfather Rong was versed in the Five Classics and expert in mathematics and water control.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Rong mastered the Five Classics and was expert in mathematics and hydraulic engineering.

sentences.zh: 時劉秉忠、張文謙、張易、王恂同學於州西紫金山，榮使守敬從秉忠學。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Bingzhong, Zhang Wenqian, Zhang Yi, and Wang Xun studied together at Purple Gold Mountain west of the prefecture; Rong had Shoujing follow Bingzhong in study.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Bingzhong, Zhang Wenqian, Zhang Yi, and Wang Xun studied together at Purple Gold Mountain west of the prefecture; Rong sent Shoujing to study under Bingzhong.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，文謙薦守敬習水利，巧思絕人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong, Wenqian recommended Shoujing as versed in water control, with ingenuity surpassing other men.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Zhongtong era Wenqian recommended Shoujing for his mastery of hydraulic engineering and ingenuity surpassing all others.

sentences.zh: 世祖召見，面陳水利六事：其一，中都舊漕河，東至通州，引玉泉水以通舟，歲可省雇車錢六萬緡。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor summoned him for an audience, and he presented in person six matters concerning water control: First, the old grain-transport canal at the Central Capital, extending east to Tongzhou—by drawing the Jade Spring water to enable passage of boats, each year some sixty thousand strings of cash in hired cart fees could be saved.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor received him in audience, and Shoujing laid out six hydraulic proposals in person. First: the old grain canal at the Central Capital, running east to Tongzhou—divert the Jade Spring to float shipping, and the realm could save sixty thousand strings of cartage every year.

sentences.zh: 通州以南，於蘭榆河口徑直開引，由蒙村跳梁務至楊村還河，以避浮雞氵甸盤淺風浪遠轉之患。

translations.literal: South of Tongzhou, at the mouth of the Lanyu River open a straight channel, from Mengcun and Tiaoliangwu to Yangcun returning to the river, to avoid the troubles of the Floating Chicken Ford's shallows, wind and waves, and long detours.
translations.idiomatic: South of Tongzhou, cut a straight intake at the Lanyu estuary, run it from Mengcun and Tiaoliangwu back to the main stream at Yangcun, and so escape the shoals of Floating Chicken Ford, the wind and waves, and the wear of long tacking.

sentences.zh: 其二，順德達泉引入城中，分為三渠，灌城東地。

translations.literal: Second, bring the Dada Spring of Shunde into the city, divide it into three canals, and irrigate the lands east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Second: lead the Dada Spring of Shunde into the city, split it into three canals, and water the ground east of the walls.

sentences.zh: 其三，順德灃河東至古任城，失其故道，沒民田千三百餘頃。

translations.literal: Third, the Feng River of Shunde east to ancient Rencheng had lost its old course and had submerged more than thirteen hundred qing of commoners' fields.
translations.idiomatic: Third: east of Shunde the Feng River toward ancient Rencheng had wandered off its old bed and drowned more than thirteen hundred qing of farmland.

sentences.zh: 此水開修成河，其田即可耕種，自小王村經滹沱，合入御河，通行舟筏。

translations.literal: If this water were opened and repaired into a river, those fields could at once be cultivated; from Little Wang Village it would pass through the Hutuo and join the Imperial Canal, allowing passage of boats and rafts.
translations.idiomatic: Reopen that water as a river and the drowned fields become arable again; from Little Wang Village route it past the Hutuo into the Imperial Canal, fit for boats and rafts.

sentences.zh: 其四，磁州東北滏、漳二水合流處，引水由滏陽、邯鄲、洺州、永年下經雞澤，合入灃河，可灌田三千餘頃。

translations.literal: Fourth, at the northeast of Cizhou where the Fu and Zhang rivers join, draw water down through Fuyang, Handan, Mingzhou, and Yongnian, passing Jize and joining the Feng River—it could irrigate more than three thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: at the confluence of the Fu and Zhang northeast of Cizhou, divert water through Fuyang, Handan, Mingzhou, and Yongnian, down past Jize into the Feng—enough to irrigate three thousand qing and more.

sentences.zh: 其五，懷、孟沁河，雖澆灌，猶有漏堰餘水，東與丹河餘水相合。

translations.literal: Fifth, the Qin River of Huai and Meng, though used for irrigation, still had surplus water leaking from the weirs, which flowed east and joined the surplus of the Dan River.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: the Qin River in Huai and Meng, for all its irrigation, still spilled weir-water eastward to meet the Dan's leftover flow.

sentences.zh: 引東流，至武陟縣北，合入御河，可灌田二千餘頃。

translations.literal: Draw it east; reaching north of Wuzhi County, let it join the Imperial Canal—it could irrigate more than two thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: Channel that eastward to north of Wuzhi, pour it into the Imperial Canal, and water another two thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 其六，黃河自孟州西開引，少分一渠，經由新、舊孟州中間，順河古岸下，至溫縣南復入大河，其間亦可灌田二千餘頃。

translations.literal: Sixth, from west of Mengzhou open a diversion on the Yellow River, dividing off a lesser canal that would pass between New and Old Mengzhou, follow the river's ancient bank downstream, and south of Wen County re-enter the Great River; in between it could also irrigate more than two thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: west of Mengzhou split the Yellow River—a lesser canal between New and Old Mengzhou, hugging the ancient levee to Wen County and back into the main stream, watering two thousand qing along the way.

sentences.zh: 每奏一事，世祖歎曰：「任事者如此，人不為素餐矣。」

translations.literal: Each time he submitted one matter, the Founding Emperor sighed and said: "When those charged with affairs are thus, men will not be eating idle provisions."
translations.idiomatic: After each proposal the Founding Emperor sighed and said, "Servants of the state like this—no one need eat for nothing."

sentences.zh: 授提舉諸路河渠。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director-in-Chief of River Works for All Routes.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director-in-Chief of River Works for All Routes.

sentences.zh: 四年，加授銀符、副河渠使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was further appointed Silver Tallies and Vice Commissioner of River Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he received the silver tally and the post of Vice Commissioner of River Works.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，從張文謙行省西夏。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan he followed Zhang Wenqian on a tour of inspection in Xixia.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiyuan he accompanied Zhang Wenqian on provincial inspection in Xixia.

sentences.zh: 先是，古渠在中興者，一名唐來，其長四百里，一名漢延，長二百五十里，它州正渠十，皆長二百里，支渠大小六十八，灌田九萬餘頃。

translations.literal: Earlier, among the ancient canals at Zhongxing, one was called Tanglai, four hundred li in length; one was called Hanyan, two hundred fifty li in length; in other prefectures there were ten main canals, each two hundred li in length, and large and small branch canals numbering sixty-eight, irrigating more than ninety thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: Before then the old canals at Zhongxing included Tanglai, four hundred li long, and Hanyan, two hundred fifty li; ten main canals in other prefectures, each two hundred li, with sixty-eight branch canals large and small, watering more than ninety thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 兵亂以來，廢壞淤淺。

translations.literal: Since the military disorders they had been abandoned, ruined, silted, and shallowed.
translations.idiomatic: War had left them broken, choked, and shallow.

sentences.zh: 守敬更立閘堰，皆復其舊。

translations.literal: Shoujing newly erected sluice-gates and weirs, and all were restored to their former state.
translations.idiomatic: Shoujing rebuilt the gates and weirs until every channel stood as before.

sentences.zh: 二年，授都水少監。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Waterworks.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was named Vice Director of the Imperial Waterworks.

sentences.zh: 守敬言：「舟自中興沿河四晝夜至東勝，可通漕運，及見查泊、兀郎海古渠甚多，宜加修理。」

translations.literal: Shoujing said: "Boats from Zhongxing along the river in four days and nights reach Dongsheng; grain transport could be opened, and moreover I have seen that at Zhabo and Ulun Hai there are many ancient canals that ought to be repaired."
translations.idiomatic: Shoujing reported, "A boat from Zhongxing can reach Dongsheng in four days and nights along the river—grain transport is feasible—and at Zhabo and Ulun Hai I found many old canals worth restoring."

sentences.zh: 又言：「金時，自燕京之西麻峪村，分引盧溝一支東流，穿西山而出，是謂金口。

translations.literal: He further said: "In Jin times, from Mayu Village west of Yanjing a branch of the Lugou was split off to flow east, piercing the Western Hills to emerge—this was called the Jinkou.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Under the Jin, west of Yanjing at Mayu Village they split the Lugou east through the Western Hills—the Jinkou.

sentences.zh: 其水自金口以東，燕京以北，灌田若干頃，其利不可勝計。

translations.literal: Its water from east of the Jinkou and north of Yanjing irrigated a certain number of qing of fields; the benefit could not be fully reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jinkou east and north of Yanjing it watered untold qing; the gain was beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 兵興以來，典守者懼有所失，因以大石塞之。

translations.literal: Since warfare arose, those in charge feared some loss and therefore blocked it with great stones.
translations.idiomatic: When war came the keepers, fearing loss, sealed it with great stones.

sentences.zh: 今若按視故跡，使水得通流，上可以致西山之利，下可以廣京畿之漕。」

translations.literal: Now if one inspects the old traces and lets the water flow through, above one could secure the benefits of the Western Hills, below one could expand grain transport in the capital region."
translations.idiomatic: Survey the old course, let the water run again, and upstream the Western Hills prosper while downstream the capital's grain routes widen."

sentences.zh: 又言：「當於金口西預開減水口，西南還大河，令其深廣，以防漲水突入之患。」

translations.literal: He further said: "At the west of the Jinkou one should beforehand open a spillway, returning southwest to the Great River and making it deep and broad, to guard against the calamity of floodwater bursting in."
translations.idiomatic: He urged also, "West of the Jinkou open a spillway beforehand, sweeping southwest back to the main river, deep and wide, lest floodwater crash through."

sentences.zh: 帝善之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 十二年，丞相伯顏南征，議立水站，命守敬行視河北、山東可通舟者，為圖奏之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when the Chancellor Bayan marched south, they discussed establishing water courier stations; the Emperor ordered Shoujing to travel and inspect Hebei and Shandong for places where boats could pass, make maps, and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, as Chancellor Bayan campaigned south, the court debated water courier stations and sent Shoujing to survey Hebei and Shandong for navigable routes, map them, and report.

sentences.zh: 初，秉忠以《大明曆》自遼、金承用二百餘年，浸以後天，議欲修正而卒。

translations.literal: Earlier, Bingzhong had held that the Great Enlightenment Calendar, inherited from Liao and Jin for more than two hundred years, had gradually lagged behind Heaven; he had discussed correcting it but died before doing so.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Bingzhong had argued that the Great Enlightenment Calendar, used by Liao and Jin for two centuries, had drifted from the sky; he meant to revise it but died with the work unfinished.

sentences.zh: 十三年，江左既平，帝思用其言，遂以守敬與王恂率南北日官，分掌測驗推步於下，而命文謙與樞密張易為之主領裁奏於上，左丞許衡參預其事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, once the Jiangzuo region was pacified, the Emperor thought to employ his words; he therefore had Shoujing and Wang Xun lead northern and southern day-officers, dividing supervision of measurement and calculation below, while ordering Wenqian and Privy Councilor Zhang Yi to take chief charge and submit decisions above, with Left Chancellor Xu Heng participating in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, with the south pacified, the Emperor took up Bingzhong's plan: Shoujing and Wang Xun led northern and southern astronomers in field measurement and computation below, while Wenqian and Privy Councilor Zhang Yi presided and reported above, and Left Chancellor Xu Heng joined the deliberations.

sentences.zh: 守敬首言：「歷之本在於測驗，而測驗之器莫先儀表。

translations.literal: Shoujing first said: "The root of the calendar lies in measurement and testing, and among instruments for testing none comes before the observational apparatus.
translations.idiomatic: Shoujing began, "A calendar lives by measurement, and measurement lives by instruments.

sentences.zh: 今司天渾儀​​，宋皇祐中汴京所造，不與此處天度相符，比量南北二極，約差四度；

translations.literal: Now the Directorate's armillary sphere was made at Bianjing in the Huangyou era of Song and does not match the celestial degrees at this place; comparing and measuring the northern and southern poles, it differs by about four degrees;
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate's armillary sphere was built at Bianjing in Song's Huangyou reign—it no longer fits our sky. Measured against the north and south poles, it errs by some four degrees;

sentences.zh: 表石年深，亦復欹側。」

translations.literal: the gnomon stone, deep in years, had likewise tilted askew."
translations.idiomatic: the gnomon stone, ancient now, had tilted as well."

sentences.zh: 守敬乃盡考其失而移置之。

translations.literal: Shoujing then fully investigated its errors and moved and reset it.
translations.idiomatic: Shoujing traced every error and repositioned the lot.

sentences.zh: 既又別圖高爽地，以木為重棚，創作簡儀、高表，用相比覆。

translations.literal: Thereafter he also separately selected high, open ground, made a heavy wooden pavilion, and newly devised the simplified instrument and the high gnomon, using them for mutual comparison and verification.
translations.idiomatic: He chose high open ground, built a heavy timber pavilion, and invented the simplified instrument and the high gnomon to cross-check one another.

sentences.zh: 又以為天樞附極而動，昔人嘗展管望之，未得其的，作候極儀。

translations.literal: He also held that the celestial pivot clings to the pole yet moves; men of old once extended tubes to sight it but did not obtain the mark, so he made the polar-waiting instrument.
translations.idiomatic: He reasoned that the celestial pivot hugs the pole yet shifts; ancients had sighted it through extended tubes without hitting true—so he made the polar-waiting instrument.

sentences.zh: 極辰既位，天體斯正，作渾天象。

translations.literal: Once the pole stars were fixed, the celestial body was thereby rectified, and he made the armillary planetarium.
translations.idiomatic: Fix the pole stars and the heavens stand true—he built the armillary planetarium.

sentences.zh: 象雖形似，莫適所用，作玲瓏儀。

translations.literal: Though the planetarium resembled the form, it suited no practical use, so he made the intricate instrument.
translations.idiomatic: The planetarium mimicked the sky but served no practical end, so he devised the intricate instrument.

sentences.zh: 以表之矩方，測天之正圜，莫若以圜求圜，作仰儀。

translations.literal: Because the gnomon's form is square while heaven's true form is round, nothing surpasses seeking the round by the round, so he made the upward-looking instrument.
translations.idiomatic: A gnomon is square and heaven truly round—best to seek the circle with circles—hence the upward-looking instrument.

sentences.zh: 古有經緯，結而不動，守敬易之，作立運儀。

translations.literal: In antiquity there were longitude and latitude rings fixed and unmoving; Shoujing changed them and made the standing revolution instrument.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity fixed longitude and latitude rings motionless; Shoujing replaced them with the standing revolution instrument.

sentences.zh: 日有中道，月有九行，守敬一之，作證理儀。

translations.literal: The sun has a middle path and the moon has nine paths; Shoujing unified them and made the principle-verifying instrument.
translations.idiomatic: The sun rides a middle path, the moon nine; Shoujing unified them in the principle-verifying instrument.

sentences.zh: 表高景虛，罔象非真，作景符。

translations.literal: When the table is high the shadow is faint and the image unreal, so he made the shadow-marker.
translations.idiomatic: Raise the table and the shadow thins to illusion—he made the shadow-marker.

sentences.zh: 月雖有明，察景則難，作窺幾。

translations.literal: Though the moon has brightness, observing the shadow is difficult, so he made the sighting-lever.
translations.idiomatic: The moon shines, yet its shadow is hard to read—he made the sighting-lever.

sentences.zh: 曆法之驗，在於交會，作日月食儀。

translations.literal: The verification of calendrical method lies in conjunction, so he made the solar and lunar eclipse instrument.
translations.idiomatic: A calendar proves itself at conjunction—he built the solar and lunar eclipse instrument.

sentences.zh: 天有赤道，輪以當之，兩極低昂，標以指之，作星晷定時儀。

translations.literal: Heaven has the equator, matched by a wheel; the two poles rise and fall, indicated by markers, so he made the star-gnomon time-setting instrument.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has an equator—a wheel to match it; the poles rise and fall—markers to point them—hence the star-gnomon time-setting instrument.

sentences.zh: 又作正方案、丸表、懸正儀、座正儀，為四方行測者所用。

translations.literal: He also made the rectifying azimuth plate, the pellet table, the suspended rectifier, and the seated rectifier, for use by those conducting measurements in the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: He also devised the rectifying azimuth plate, pellet table, suspended rectifier, and seated rectifier for observers in every quarter.

sentences.zh: 又作《仰規覆矩圖》、《異方渾蓋圖》、《日出入永短圖》，與上諸儀互相參考。

translations.literal: He also made the Upward Rule and Inverted Square Diagram, the Different Regions Armillary Cover Diagram, and the Sun's Rising and Setting and Length Diagram, for mutual reference with the instruments above.
translations.idiomatic: He drew the Upward Rule and Inverted Square, Different Regions Armillary Cover, and Sun's Rising, Setting, and Length charts to cross-reference the instruments.

sentences.zh: 十六年，改局為太史院，以恂為太史令，守敬為同知太史院事，給印章，立官府。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the bureau was changed to the Grand Astrologer's Court; Xun was made Grand Astrologer, Shoujing Associate Administrator of the Grand Astrologer's Court; seals were granted and an official office established.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the bureau became the Grand Astrologer's Court: Xun as Grand Astrologer, Shoujing as associate administrator—seals issued, offices founded.

sentences.zh: 及奏進儀表式，守敬當帝前指陳理致，至於日晏，帝不為倦。

translations.literal: When the models of instruments were submitted, Shoujing before the Emperor pointed and explained their principles, until the sun stood at dusk, and the Emperor was not weary.
translations.idiomatic: When the instrument models were presented, Shoujing explained their principles before the throne until dusk, and the Emperor never tired.

sentences.zh: 守敬因奏：「唐一行開元間令南宮說天下測景，書中見者凡十三處。

translations.literal: Shoujing thereupon memorialized: "In the Kaiyuan era Tang Yixing ordered Nangong Shuo to measure shadows throughout the realm; those recorded in books number thirteen places in all.
translations.idiomatic: Shoujing then memorialized, "In Kaiyuan the Tang calendrist Yixing sent Nangong Shuo to measure shadows empire-wide—thirteen sites appear in the books.

sentences.zh: 今疆宇比唐尤大，若不遠方測驗，日月交食分數時刻不同，晝夜長短不同，日月星辰去天高下不同，即目測驗人少，可先南北立表，取直測景。」

translations.literal: Today's territory is even greater than Tang's; if one does not test at distant places, the degrees and times of solar and lunar eclipses will differ, day and night lengths will differ, and the heights of sun, moon, and stars from heaven will differ; since for immediate testing there are few men, one may first erect gnomons north and south and take straight shadow measurements."
translations.idiomatic: Our realm exceeds Tang's; without distant measurements, eclipse magnitudes and times, day and night lengths, and the heights of sun, moon, and stars will all diverge. With too few observers at hand, set gnomons north and south first and measure shadows directly."

sentences.zh: 帝可其奏。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 遂設監候官一十四員，分道而出，東至高麗，西極滇池，南逾硃崖，北盡鐵勒，四海測驗，凡二十七所。

translations.literal: Thereupon fourteen supervising observers were established, each taking a separate route: east to Goryeo, west to the end of Dian Lake, south beyond Zhuya, north to the limit of Tiele; throughout the four seas measurements were taken, twenty-seven places in all.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen supervising observers were sent out by separate routes—east to Goryeo, west to Dian Pool, south past Zhuya, north to Tiele's edge—twenty-seven stations measuring under all four seas.

sentences.zh: 十七年，新歷告成，守敬與諸臣同上奏曰：

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the new calendar was completed; Shoujing together with the ministers jointly submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the new calendar was finished; Shoujing and the ministers jointly memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣等竊聞帝王之事，莫重於歷。

translations.literal: We your subjects have heard that among the affairs of emperors and kings, none is heavier than the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly hear that among the labors of emperors and kings, none weighs more than the calendar.

sentences.zh: 自黃帝迎日推策，帝堯以閏月定四時成歲，舜在璇璣玉衡以齊七政。

translations.literal: From the Yellow Emperor, who welcomed the sun and pushed the counting rods, Emperor Yao, who by intercalary months fixed the four seasons to complete the year, and Shun, who with the armillary sphere of jade and the leveling tube aligned the seven regulators.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor welcomed the sun and cast the rods; Yao fixed the four seasons with intercalary months; Shun aligned the seven regulators with the jade armillary and leveling tube.

sentences.zh: 爰及三代，歷無定法，周、秦之間，閏餘乖次。

translations.literal: Down through the Three Dynasties the calendar had no fixed method; between Zhou and Qin the intercalary remainder fell out of sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Three Dynasties calendars lacked fixed law; between Zhou and Qin intercalary remainders lost their order.

sentences.zh: 西漢造《三統曆》，百三十年而後是非始定。

translations.literal: In Western Han the Triple Concordance Calendar was made; only after one hundred thirty years were right and wrong first settled.
translations.idiomatic: Western Han produced the Triple Concordance Calendar; a hundred thirty years passed before right and wrong were settled.

sentences.zh: 東漢造《四分曆》，七十餘年而儀式方備。

translations.literal: In Eastern Han the Quarter-Remainder Calendar was made; only after more than seventy years were the instruments and procedures complete.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han produced the Quarter-Remainder Calendar; seventy years more before instruments and rites were complete.

sentences.zh: 又百二十一年，劉洪造《乾象曆》，始悟月行有遲速。

translations.literal: After another one hundred twenty-one years Liu Hong made the Supernal Manifestation Calendar and first understood that the moon's motion has fast and slow phases.
translations.idiomatic: Another hundred twenty-one years: Liu Hong's Supernal Manifestation Calendar first grasped that the moon speeds and slows.

sentences.zh: 又百八十年，姜岌造《三紀甲子曆》，始悟以月食衝檢日宿度所在。

translations.literal: After another one hundred eighty years Jiang Ji made the Triple Era Jiazi Calendar and first understood using lunar eclipse opposition to test the lodge-degrees where the sun stands.
translations.idiomatic: Another hundred eighty: Jiang Ji's Triple Era Jiazi Calendar first used lunar eclipse opposition to fix the sun's lodge and degree.

sentences.zh: 又五十七年，何承天造《元嘉曆》，始悟以朔望及弦皆定大小餘。

translations.literal: After another fifty-seven years He Chengtian made the Origin of Blessing Calendar and first understood fixing the greater and lesser remainders for new moon, full moon, and the two quarters alike.
translations.idiomatic: Another fifty-seven: He Chengtian's Origin of Blessing Calendar first fixed greater and lesser remainders for new, full, and both quarters alike.

sentences.zh: 又六十五年，祖沖之造《大明曆》，始悟太陽有歲差之數，極星去不動處一度餘。

translations.literal: After another sixty-five years Zu Chongzhi made the Great Enlightenment Calendar and first understood that the sun has a precessional number and the pole star is more than one degree from the unmoving place.
translations.idiomatic: Another sixty-five: Zu Chongzhi's Great Enlightenment Calendar first measured the sun's precession and found the pole star more than a degree from the fixed point.

sentences.zh: 又五十二年，張子信始悟日月交道有表裡，五星有遲疾留逆。

translations.literal: After another fifty-two years Zhang Zixin first understood that the sun-moon crossing has inner and outer aspects and the five stars have fast, slow, station, and retrograde motions.
translations.idiomatic: Another fifty-two: Zhang Zixin first saw that the sun-moon path has inner and outer faces and the five stars hurry, linger, halt, and retreat.

sentences.zh: 又三十三年，劉焯造《皇極曆》，始悟日行有盈縮。

translations.literal: After another thirty-three years Liu Zhuo made the Imperial Ultimate Calendar and first understood that the sun's daily motion has expansion and contraction.
translations.idiomatic: Another thirty-three: Liu Zhuo's Imperial Ultimate Calendar first caught the sun's daily motion in expansion and contraction.

sentences.zh: 又三十五年，傅仁均造《戊寅元曆》，頗採舊儀，始用定朔。

translations.literal: After another thirty-five years Fu Renjun made the Wuyin Origin Calendar, broadly adopting old procedures and first using fixed new moons.
translations.idiomatic: Another thirty-five: Fu Renjun's Wuyin Origin Calendar drew on old rites and first employed fixed new moons.

sentences.zh: 又四十六年，李淳風造《麟德曆》，以古歷章蔀元首分度不齊，始為總法，用進朔以避晦晨月見。

translations.literal: After another forty-six years Li Chunfeng made the Virtue of Lin Calendar; because in ancient calendars the rule, obscuration, origin, and head and their degree divisions were not uniform, he first made a general method and used advancing the new moon to avoid the moon visible on the last morning of the month.
translations.idiomatic: Another forty-six: Li Chunfeng's Virtue of Lin Calendar, finding ancient rule, obscuration, origin, and head degrees inconsistent, devised a general method and advanced the new moon to keep the moon from showing on the month's last dawn.

sentences.zh: 又六十三年，一行造《大衍曆》，始以朔有四大三小，定九服交食之異。

translations.literal: After another sixty-three years Yixing made the Great Expansion Calendar and first took that among new moons four are large and three small, fixing the differences of eclipse across the nine domains.
translations.idiomatic: Another sixty-three: Yixing's Great Expansion Calendar first reckoned four long and three short months among the new moons and fixed eclipse variation across the nine domains.

sentences.zh: 又九十四年，徐昂造《宣明曆》，始悟日食有氣、刻、時三差。

translations.literal: After another ninety-four years Xu Ang made the Manifest Brightness Calendar and first understood that solar eclipses have three differences of vapor, mark, and time.
translations.idiomatic: Another ninety-four: Xu Ang's Manifest Brightness Calendar first distinguished solar eclipses by vapor, mark, and time.

sentences.zh: 又二百三十六年，姚舜輔造《紀元曆》，始悟食甚泛餘差數。

translations.literal: After another two hundred thirty-six years Yao Shunfu made the Era Origin Calendar and first understood the surplus-difference numbers at greatest eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Another two hundred thirty-six: Yao Shunfu's Era Origin Calendar first mastered the surplus-difference at greatest eclipse.

sentences.zh: 以上計千一百八十二年，歷經七十改，其創法者十有三家。

translations.literal: The above totals one thousand one hundred eighty-two years, seventy revisions of the calendar, and thirteen houses that created methods.
translations.idiomatic: In all: one thousand one hundred eighty-two years, seventy calendar reforms, thirteen founders of new methods.

sentences.zh: 自是又百七十四年，聖朝專命臣等改治新歷，臣等用創造簡儀、高表，憑其測實數，所考正者凡七事：

translations.literal: From then another one hundred seventy-four years have passed, and the sage court specially ordered us your subjects to reform and make a new calendar; we your subjects used the newly devised simplified instrument and high gnomon, relying on their measured true numbers, and what we examined and corrected number seven matters in all:
translations.idiomatic: Another hundred seventy-four years on, the sage court charged us to forge a new calendar. With the simplified instrument and high gnomon we measured true numbers and corrected seven matters:

sentences.zh: 一曰冬至。

translations.literal: First, the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: First: the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 自丙子年立冬後，依每日測到晷景，逐日取對，冬至前後日差同者為準。

translations.literal: From after the start of winter in the bingzi year, according to gnomon shadows measured daily, taking day-by-day correspondences, those with equal day-differences before and after the winter solstice were taken as standard.
translations.idiomatic: From winter's onset in the bingzi year we measured the gnomon shadow daily and paired successive days; where the day-difference matched before and after solstice, that marked the instant.

sentences.zh: 得丁丑年冬至在戊戌日夜半後八刻半，又定丁丑夏至在庚子日夜半後七十刻；

translations.literal: We obtained that the winter solstice of the dingzi year fell on the wuxu day, eight and a half marks after midnight; we also fixed the summer solstice of dingzi on the gengzi day, seventy marks after midnight;
translations.idiomatic: Thus dingzi's winter solstice fell on wuxu, eight and a half marks past midnight; dingzi's summer solstice on gengzi, seventy marks past midnight;

sentences.zh: 又定戊寅冬至在癸卯日夜半後三十三刻；

translations.literal: we further fixed the winter solstice of wuyin on the guimao day, thirty-three marks after midnight;
translations.idiomatic: wuyin's winter solstice on guimao, thirty-three marks past midnight;

sentences.zh: 己卯冬至在戊申日夜半後五十七刻半；

translations.literal: the winter solstice of jimao on the wushen day, fifty-seven and a half marks after midnight;
translations.idiomatic: jimao's on wushen, fifty-seven and a half marks past midnight;

sentences.zh: 庚辰冬至在癸丑日夜半後八十一刻半。

translations.literal: the winter solstice of gengchen on the guichou day, eighty-one and a half marks after midnight.
translations.idiomatic: gengchen's on guichou, eighty-one and a half marks past midnight.

sentences.zh: 各減《大明曆》十八刻，遠近相符，前後應準。

translations.literal: Each reduced the Great Enlightenment Calendar by eighteen marks; near and far agreed, before and after matched the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Each was eighteen marks earlier than the Great Enlightenment Calendar—near and far aligned, past and future matched.

sentences.zh: 二曰歲餘。

translations.literal: Second, the year surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Second: the tropical year surplus.

sentences.zh: 自《大明曆》以來，凡測景、驗氣，得冬至時刻真數者有六，用以相距，各得其時合用歲餘。

translations.literal: Since the Great Enlightenment Calendar, in all shadow measurement and qi verification, six true winter-solstice instants were obtained; using them to measure intervals, each yielded the year surplus proper to its time.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Great Enlightenment Calendar, six true winter solstices from shadow and qi tests, spaced apart, each yielded its proper year surplus.

sentences.zh: 今考驗四年，相符不差，仍自宋大明壬寅年距至今日八百一十年，每歲合得三百六十五日二十四刻二十五分，其二十五分為今歷歲餘合用之數。

translations.literal: Now tested over four years, they agree without discrepancy; still, from the renyin year of Song's Daming to today is eight hundred ten years; each year should yield three hundred sixty-five days, twenty-four marks, and twenty-five parts—and the twenty-five parts are the year surplus proper to the present calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Four years of verification agree to a hair; from Song Daming's renyin year to today is eight hundred ten years—each year three hundred sixty-five days, twenty-four marks, twenty-five parts, and those twenty-five parts are the surplus our calendar adopts.

sentences.zh: 三曰日躔。

translations.literal: Third, the sun's lodge-transit.
translations.idiomatic: Third: the sun's lodge-transit.

sentences.zh: 用至元丁丑四月癸酉望月食既，推求日躔，得冬至日躔赤道箕宿十度，黃道箕九度有奇。

translations.literal: Using the total lunar eclipse on the guiyou day of the fourth month of dingzi in Zhiyuan, we sought the sun's lodge-transit and obtained that at the winter solstice the sun lodged at ten degrees of the equatorial Winnowing Basket, and at nine odd degrees of the ecliptic Winnowing Basket.
translations.idiomatic: From the total lunar eclipse on dingzi's fourth-month guiyou in Zhiyuan we derived the sun's position: at winter solstice ten degrees equatorial Winnowing Basket, nine and a fraction ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 仍憑每日測到太陽躔度，或憑星測月，或憑月測日，或徑憑星度測日，立術推算。

translations.literal: Still relying on the sun's lodge-transit measured daily, or measuring the moon by stars, or measuring the sun by the moon, or directly measuring the sun by star degrees, we established methods to calculate.
translations.idiomatic: Daily solar positions, or stars on the moon, moon on the sun, stars on the sun directly—we built methods for each.

sentences.zh: 起自丁丑正月至己卯十二月，凡三年，共得一百三十四事，皆躔於箕，與月食相符。

translations.literal: From the first month of dingzi to the twelfth month of jimao, three years in all, one hundred thirty-four cases were obtained, all lodging in Winnowing Basket, agreeing with the lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: From dingzi's first month through jimao's twelfth—three years, one hundred thirty-four cases—all in Winnowing Basket, matching the eclipse.

sentences.zh: 四曰月離。

translations.literal: Fourth, the moon's departure.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: the moon's departure.

sentences.zh: 自丁丑以來至今，憑每日測到逐時太陰行度推算，變從黃道求入轉極遲、疾並平行處，前後凡十三轉，計五十一事。

translations.literal: From dingzi to the present, according to the moon's hourly motion measured daily, calculating by change from the ecliptic to seek the places of entry into rotation, extreme slow, fast, and mean motion, thirteen rotations in all before and after, totaling fifty-one cases.
translations.idiomatic: From dingzi onward, hourly lunar motion measured daily, converted along the ecliptic to find entry into rotation, extremes of slow and fast, and mean motion—thirteen cycles, fifty-one cases in all.

sentences.zh: 內除去不真的外，有三十事，得《大明曆》入轉後天。

translations.literal: Within, excluding those not true, there were thirty cases, showing that the Great Enlightenment Calendar's entry into rotation lags behind Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty reliable cases proved the Great Enlightenment Calendar's rotation entry lags heaven.

sentences.zh: 又因考驗交食，加《大明曆》三十刻，與天道合。

translations.literal: Moreover, by testing conjunction eclipses, thirty marks were added to the Great Enlightenment Calendar, matching the Way of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipse tests added thirty marks to the Great Enlightenment Calendar—now it matches heaven's way.

sentences.zh: 五曰入交。

translations.literal: Fifth, entry into crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: entry into crossing.

sentences.zh: 自丁丑五月以來，憑每日測到太陰去極度數，比擬黃道去極度，得月道交於黃道，共得八事。

translations.literal: From the fifth month of dingzi onward, according to the moon's polar distance measured daily, compared with the ecliptic's polar distance, the moon's path crossing the ecliptic was obtained—eight cases in all.
translations.idiomatic: From dingzi's fifth month, daily lunar polar distance against the ecliptic's yielded eight crossings of the moon's path with the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 仍依日食法度推求，皆有食分，得入交時刻，與《大明曆》所差不多。

translations.literal: Still, by the methods and degrees of solar eclipse we sought calculation; all had eclipse magnitude; the instants of entry into crossing were obtained, differing little from those of the Great Enlightenment Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Solar-eclipse methods gave magnitude and crossing instant for each—little different from the Great Enlightenment Calendar.

sentences.zh: 六曰二十八宿距度。

translations.literal: Sixth, the interval-degrees of the twenty-eight lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: the twenty-eight lodges' interval-degrees.

sentences.zh: 自漢《太初曆》以來，距度不同，互有損益。

translations.literal: Since the Han Grand Inception Calendar, interval-degrees have differed, each increasing or decreasing the other.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han's Grand Inception, lodge intervals have shifted, each calendar adding or subtracting.

sentences.zh: 《大明曆》則於度下餘分，附以太半少，皆私意牽就，未嘗實測其數。

translations.literal: The Great Enlightenment Calendar, for the fractional parts below the degree, attached a great half and a little less—all forced by private intent, never actually measuring the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Enlightenment Calendar padded fractional parts with "great half, little less"—private fudge, never measured.

sentences.zh: 今新儀皆細刻周天度分，每度分三十六分，以距線代管窺，宿度餘分並依實測，不以私意牽就。

translations.literal: Now the new instruments finely mark the degrees and parts of the full circuit of heaven; each degree is divided into thirty-six parts; interval-lines replace tube-sighting; lodge-degree fractional parts all follow actual measurement, not forced by private intent.
translations.idiomatic: Our new instruments mark the full circuit fine: thirty-six parts per degree, interval-lines instead of tube-sighting, lodge fractions from measurement—not private forcing.

sentences.zh: 七曰日出入晝夜刻。

translations.literal: Seventh, the marks of sunrise, sunset, day, and night.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: sunrise, sunset, day, and night marks.

sentences.zh: 《大明曆》日出入夜晝刻，皆據汴京為準，其刻數與大都不同。

translations.literal: The Great Enlightenment Calendar's marks for sunset, sunrise, night, and day all took Bianjing as standard; the mark-numbers differ from those of Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Enlightenment Calendar reckoned day and night from Bianjing; Dadu's numbers differ.

sentences.zh: 今更以本方北極出地高下，黃道出入內外度，立術推求每日日出入晝夜刻，得夏至極長，日出寅正二刻，日入戌初二刻，晝六十二刻，夜三十八刻。

translations.literal: Now, further using this region's height of the north pole above the earth, and the degrees of the ecliptic's entry inner and outer, we established methods to seek the daily marks of sunrise, sunset, day, and night; we obtained that at the summer solstice, when day is longest, the sun rises at the second mark of yin proper, sets at the second mark of xu initial, day sixty-two marks, night thirty-eight marks.
translations.idiomatic: We recalculated from this site's polar height and the ecliptic's inner and outer limits: at summer solstice, longest day, sun rises at yin proper's second mark, sets at xu initial's second, sixty-two marks of day, thirty-eight of night.

sentences.zh: 冬至極短，日出辰初二刻，日入申正二刻，晝三十八刻，夜六十二刻。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice, when day is shortest, the sun rises at the second mark of chen initial, sets at the second mark of shen proper, day thirty-eight marks, night sixty-two marks.
translations.idiomatic: At winter solstice, shortest day, sun rises at chen initial's second mark, sets at shen proper's second, thirty-eight marks of day, sixty-two of night.

sentences.zh: 永為定式。

translations.literal: These shall forever be the fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Let these stand as the fixed pattern forever.

sentences.zh: 所創法凡五事：一曰太陽盈縮。

translations.literal: The methods newly created number five matters in all: first, solar expansion and contraction.
translations.idiomatic: The new methods number five in all: first, solar expansion and contraction.

sentences.zh: 用四正定氣立為升降限，依立招差求得每日行分初末極差積度，比古為密。

translations.literal: Using the four rectified fixed qi to establish limits of ascent and descent, and by finite-difference interpolation to obtain each day's motion parts, initial and final, extreme differences, and accumulated degrees, it is finer than the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: The four rectified qi set the bounds of solar rise and fall; finite-difference interpolation yields each day's motion, its extremes, and cumulative degrees—finer than any ancient calendar.

sentences.zh: 二曰月行遲疾。

translations.literal: Second: the moon's slow and fast motion.
translations.idiomatic: Second: the moon's variable speed.

sentences.zh: 古歷皆用二十八限，今以萬分日之八百二十分為一限，凡析為三百三十六限，依垛疊招差求得轉分進退，其遲疾度數逐時不同，蓋前所未有。

translations.literal: Ancient calendars all used twenty-eight limits; now eight hundred twenty parts of ten thousand parts of a day make one limit, divided in all into three hundred thirty-six limits; by piled finite-difference interpolation the turning parts of advance and retreat are obtained; the degrees of slowness and speed differ from moment to moment—something never before seen.
translations.idiomatic: Older calendars used twenty-eight limits; the new one sets one limit at 820 parts in 10,000 of a day, subdivided into 336 limits. Piled finite-difference interpolation yields the moon's shifting motion; its slow-fast degrees change hour by hour—unprecedented.

sentences.zh: 三曰黃赤道差。

translations.literal: Third: ecliptic-equatorial difference.
translations.idiomatic: Third: the ecliptic-equatorial correction.

sentences.zh: 舊法以一百一度相減相乘，今依算術句股弧矢方圜斜直所容，求到度率積差，差率與天道實吻合。

translations.literal: The old method used one hundred one degrees in mutual subtraction and multiplication; now, following arithmetic of right triangles, arc and chord, square and circle, oblique and straight containment, the degree-rates and accumulated differences are obtained; the difference-rates truly accord with the Way of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The old method merely subtracted and multiplied by 101 degrees; the new reckoning uses gnomon-triangle, arc-chord, and circle-square geometry to derive degree-rates and cumulative difference—rates that match heaven's course.

sentences.zh: 四曰黃赤道內外度。

translations.literal: Fourth: ecliptic-equatorial inner and outer degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: inner and outer ecliptic-equatorial limits.

sentences.zh: 據累年實測，內外極度二十三度九十分，以圜容方直矢接句股為法，求每日去極，與所測相符。
