translations.literal: According to accumulated years of actual measurement, the inner and outer polar limits are twenty-three degrees ninety parts; taking circle-containing-square, straight arrow, and connected right triangles as method, the daily distance from the pole is sought and agrees with what was measured.
translations.idiomatic: Years of observation fixed the polar limits at 23°90'; circle-square and arrow-chord methods now yield each day's polar distance in agreement with the measures.

sentences.zh: 五曰白道交周。

translations.literal: Fifth: white-path nodal circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: the lunar path's nodal cycle.

sentences.zh: 舊法黃道變推白道以斜求斜，今用立渾比量，得月與赤道正交，距春秋二正黃赤道正交一十四度六十六分，擬以為法。

translations.literal: The old method transformed the ecliptic to derive the white path and sought obliquely by obliquity; now the armillary sphere is set up for comparison and measurement, obtaining the moon's right crossing with the equator at a distance of fourteen degrees sixty-six parts from the spring and autumn equinoctial crossings of yellow and red, taken as the pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Older methods derived the lunar path from the ecliptic by oblique reckoning; the new method uses the armillary sphere and finds the moon crossing the equator 14°66' from the spring and autumn equinoxes—taken as the norm.

sentences.zh: 推逐月每交二十八宿度分，於理為盡。

translations.literal: Calculating month by month each crossing's degrees and parts among the twenty-eight lodges, in principle nothing is left out.
translations.idiomatic: Month by month it computes each nodal crossing through the twenty-eight lodges to the last degree—nothing left unresolved.

sentences.zh: 十九年，恂卒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Xun died.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Wang Xun died.

sentences.zh: 時歷雖頒，然其推步之式與夫立成之數，尚皆未有定稿。

translations.literal: At that time, though the calendar had been promulgated, its computational procedures and the numbers of the ready-made tables still had no final draft.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar was already in force, yet its computational formulas and table constants still lacked a finished draft.

sentences.zh: 守敬於是比次篇類，整齊分杪，裁為《推步》七卷，《立成》二卷，《歷議擬稿》三卷，《轉神選擇》二卷，《上中下三歷注式》十二卷。

translations.literal: Shoujing thereupon arranged the sections by category, put parts and seconds in order, and reduced them to Ephemeris Calculation in seven juan, Tabular Constants in two juan, Draft Calendar Discourse in three juan, Turning Spirit Selection in two juan, and Commentarial Forms for Upper, Middle, and Lower Calendars in twelve juan.
translations.idiomatic: Shoujing then sorted the materials by topic, harmonized every fraction, and produced Ephemeris Calculation (7 juan), Tabular Constants (2 juan), Draft Calendar Discourse (3 juan), Turning Spirit Selection (2 juan), and Commentarial Forms for the Three Calendars (12 juan).

sentences.zh: 二十三年，繼為太史令，遂上表奏進。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he succeeded as Director of the Astronomy Bureau and thereupon submitted a memorial to present them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he became Director of the Astronomy Bureau and memorialized the throne with the completed works.

sentences.zh: 又有《時候箋注》二卷，《修改源流》一卷。

translations.literal: There were also Seasonal Notes in two juan and Sources of Revision in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Seasonal Notes (2 juan) and Sources of Revision (1 juan).

sentences.zh: 其測驗書，有《儀像法式》二卷，《二至晷景考》二十卷，《五星細行考五十卷》，《古今交食考》一卷，《新測二十八舍雜坐諸星入宿去極》一卷，《新測無名諸星》一卷，《月離考》一卷，並藏之官。

translations.literal: His books of verification were Design of Astronomical Instruments in two juan, Investigation of Solstice and Equinox Gnomon Shadows in twenty juan, Investigation of the Fine Motions of the Five Stars in fifty juan, Investigation of Eclipses Past and Present in one juan, New Measurement of the Lodges and Miscellaneous Stars Entering Lodges and Polar Distance in one juan, New Measurement of Unnamed Stars in one juan, and Investigation of Lunar Separation in one juan—all deposited in the government archives.
translations.idiomatic: His observational treatises included Design of Astronomical Instruments (2 juan), Solstice and Equinox Shadow Studies (20 juan), Fine Motions of the Five Planets (50 juan), Eclipses Past and Present (1 juan), New Lodge and Star Positions (1 juan), New Unnamed Stars (1 juan), and Lunar Separation (1 juan)—all kept in the imperial archives.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，有言灤河自永平挽舟逾山而上，可至開平；

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year someone said that on the Luan River from Yongping one could tow boats over the mountains up to Kaiping;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year some proposed hauling boats up the Luan River from Yongping over the mountains to Kaiping;

sentences.zh: 有言瀘溝自麻峪可至尋麻林。

translations.literal: someone said that from Mayu on the Lugou one could reach Xunmalin.
translations.idiomatic: others that the Lugou canal from Mayu could reach Xunmalin.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣守敬相視，灤河既不可行，瀘溝舟亦不通守敬因陳水利十有一事。

translations.literal: The court sent Shoujing to inspect on site; the Luan route could not be used, and boats on the Lugou also could not pass. Shoujing thereupon submitted eleven items on water control.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Shoujing to survey both routes. The Luan was impracticable and Lugou traffic impossible; he then memorialized eleven hydraulic projects.

sentences.zh: 其一，大都運糧河，不用一畝泉舊原，別引北山白浮泉水，西折而南，經甕山泊，自西水門入城，環匯於積水潭，復東折而南，出南水門，合入舊運糧河。

translations.literal: The first: for the Dadu grain-transport canal, do not use the old course of the Yimu Spring; separately draw the Baifu Spring from the northern hills, bend it west then south, pass Wengshan Lake, enter the city through the West Water Gate, encircle and gather at Jishuitan, bend east then south again, and leave through the South Water Gate to join the old grain-transport canal.
translations.idiomatic: First: for Dadu's grain canal, abandon the old Yimu Spring line and divert Baifu Spring from the northern hills west and south through Wengshan Lake into the West Water Gate, around Jishuitan, then out the South Water Gate to rejoin the old transport channel.

sentences.zh: 每十里置一閘，比至通州，凡為閘七，距閘里許，上重置斗門，互為提閼，以過舟止水。

translations.literal: Every ten li a sluice was set; reaching Tongzhou there were seven sluices in all; about a li from each sluice an upper flash lock was reset, mutually raising and closing to pass boats and hold back water.
translations.idiomatic: A lock every ten li—seven in all to Tongzhou—with flash locks a li upstream of each, alternating to lift boats and dam the flow.

sentences.zh: 帝覽奏，喜曰：「當速行之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor perused the memorial and said with pleasure, "It should be carried out at once."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor read the memorial and said gladly, "Carry this out at once."

sentences.zh: 於是復置都水監，俾守敬領之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Directorate of Waterways was re-established and Shoujing was put in charge.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Waterways was restored and Shoujing placed at its head.

sentences.zh: 帝命丞相以下皆親操畚鍤倡工，待守敬指授而後行事。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered everyone from the chief counselor down to take spades and hoes personally to lead the labor, acting only after Shoujing's instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the chief counselor and all below to wield spade and hoe at the worksite themselves, and none might move until Shoujing directed them.

sentences.zh: 先是，通州至大都，陸運官糧，歲若干萬石，方秋霖雨，驢畜死者不可勝計，至是皆罷之。

translations.literal: Previously, from Tongzhou to Dadu official grain was transported overland—several ten thousands of piculs yearly; in autumn's long rains pack animals died beyond counting; from this time all that was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Before, tens of thousands of piculs yearly went by land from Tongzhou to Dadu; in autumn rains donkeys and oxen died beyond count. That burden was now lifted.

sentences.zh: 三十年，帝還自上都，過積水潭，見舳艫敝水，大悅，名曰通惠河，賜守敬鈔萬二千五百貫，仍以舊職兼提調通惠河漕運事。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the Emperor returned from Shangdu, passed Jishuitan, saw boats crowding the water, and was greatly pleased; he named it the Tonghui Canal, granted Shoujing twelve thousand five hundred strings of paper money, and still in his former office additionally supervised Tonghui grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, returning from Shangdu, he passed Jishuitan, saw boats packed on the water, and rejoiced. He named the canal Tonghui, gave Shoujing 12,500 strings of cash, and left him in office to oversee its transport.

sentences.zh: 守敬又言：於澄清閘稍東，引水與北霸河接，且立閘麗正門西，令舟楫得環城往來。

translations.literal: Shoujing also said that slightly east of Chengqing Sluice water should be led to join the North Ba River, and a sluice set west of Lizheng Gate so that boats could circle the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shoujing also proposed diverting water east of Chengqing Lock into the North Ba River and building a lock west of Lizheng Gate so craft could circle the capital.

sentences.zh: 志不就而罷。

translations.literal: The plan was not completed and was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was never finished and was dropped.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，拜昭文館大學士、知太史院事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was appointed Academician of the Hall for the Veneration of Literature and given charge of the Astronomy Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was made Academician of the Hall for the Veneration of Literature and head of the Astronomy Bureau.

sentences.zh: 大德二年，召守敬至上都，議開鐵幡竿渠，守敬奏：「山水頻年暴下，非大為渠堰，廣五七十步不可。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade Shoujing was summoned to Shangdu to discuss opening the Iron Banner Pole Canal; Shoujing memorialized: "Mountains and rivers have burst down violently year after year; unless canals and dikes are built on a great scale, fifty or seventy paces wide, it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 2 Shoujing was called to Shangdu to open the Iron Banner Pole Canal. He memorialized, "Floods have thundered down these mountains year after year; unless we build channels and dikes fifty or seventy paces wide, we cannot hold them."

sentences.zh: 執政吝於工費，以其言為過，縮其廣三之一。

translations.literal: The chief ministers were stingy with labor costs, took his words as excessive, and reduced the width by one-third.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers grudged the expense, called him extravagant, and cut the width by a third.

sentences.zh: 明年大雨，山水注下，渠不能容，漂沒人畜廬帳，幾犯行殿。

translations.literal: The next year great rain fell; mountains and rivers poured down; the canal could not contain them and drowned people, livestock, huts, and tents, nearly reaching the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Next year came torrential rains; the channel overflowed, drowning people, herds, and camps almost to the imperial lodge.

sentences.zh: 成宗謂宰臣曰：「郭太史神人也，惜其言不用耳。」

translations.literal: Emperor Chengzong said to his ministers, "Grand Astrologer Guo is a divine man; alas that his words were not used."
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong told his ministers, "Grand Astrologer Guo is a prophet; pity we did not heed him."

sentences.zh: 七年，詔內外官年及七十，並聽致仕，獨守敬不許其請。

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict allowed all inner and outer officials who reached seventy to retire, but Shoujing alone was not permitted his request.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the court let officials at seventy retire—except Shoujing, whose petition was refused.

sentences.zh: 自是翰林太史司天官不致仕，定著為令。

translations.literal: From this the Hanlin, Astronomy Bureau, and Directorate of Astronomy were fixed by statute not to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Hanlin and astronomical offices were barred from retirement by permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 延祐三年卒，年八十六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanyou he died, aged eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yanyou 3, aged eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 楊桓，字武子，兗州人。

translations.literal: Yang Huan, styled Wuzi, was a native of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huan, courtesy name Wuzi, was from Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼警悟，讀《論語》至《宰予晝寢章》，慨然有立志，由是終身非疾病未嘗晝寢。

translations.literal: In youth he was keen and perceptive; reading the Analects to the chapter on Zai Yu napping by day, he was moved to set his will and thereafter all his life, unless ill, never slept by day.
translations.idiomatic: Clever as a boy, he read the Analects to Zai Yu's midday sleep, resolved on the spot, and thereafter never napped except in sickness.

sentences.zh: 弱冠為郡諸生，一時名公咸稱譽之。

translations.literal: At weak cap he became a district student; for a time all eminent men praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he became a district student, and leading men praised him everywhere.

sentences.zh: 中統四年，補濟州教授，後由濟寧路教授召為太史院校書郎，奉敕撰《儀表銘》《曆日序》，文辭典雅，賜楮幣千五百緡，辭不受。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongtong he was appointed professor at Jizhou; later, from professor of Jining Route he was summoned as collator of the Astronomy Bureau, received an order to compose Inscriptions for Astronomical Instruments and Preface to the Calendar Day, his literary style elegant; he was granted one thousand five hundred min of paper money and declined it.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 4 he became professor at Jizhou; later, as Jining professor, he entered the Astronomy Bureau to draft Inscriptions for Astronomical Instruments and Preface to the Calendar Day—elegant work—and refused 1,500 min of paper money.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書監丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to assistant director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to assistant director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 至元三十一年，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Zhiyuan he was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 31 he became investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 有得玉璽於木華黎曾孫碩德家者，桓辨識其文，曰「受天之命，既壽永昌」，乃頓首言曰：「此歷代傳國璽也，亡之久矣。

translations.literal: When a jade seal was obtained in the house of Muqali's great-grandson Shuo De, Huan identified the inscription and said, "Received Heaven's command; long life and eternal stability," then bowed his head and said, "This is the imperial seal transmitted through successive dynasties; it has been lost for long.
translations.idiomatic: When a jade seal turned up in the home of Muqali's great-grandson Shuo De, Huan read its text—"Received Heaven's command; long life and eternal stability"—kowtowed, and said, "This is the dynastic seal of state, lost for ages.

sentences.zh: 今宮車晏駕，皇太孫龍飛，而璽復出，天其彰瑞應於今日乎！」

translations.literal: Now the imperial carriage rests in peace, the imperial great-grandson soars as dragon, yet the seal appears again—does Heaven not manifest this auspicious response upon today!"
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's bier is still warm, the heir-apparent has taken flight—and the seal returns. Does Heaven not show its favor upon this day?"

sentences.zh: 即為文述璽始末，奉上於徽仁裕聖皇后。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed a text setting forth the seal's beginning and end and presented it to Empress Zhiren Yusheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote an account of the seal from first to last and presented it to Empress Zhiren Yusheng.

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，桓疏上時務二十一事：一曰郊祀天地；

translations.literal: When Chengzong took the throne, Huan submitted a memorial on twenty-one affairs of the time: first, sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the suburban altars;
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong ascended, Huan memorialized twenty-one reforms: first, suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth;

sentences.zh: 二曰親享太廟，備四時之祭；

translations.literal: second, personally perform sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, providing the four seasons' offerings;
translations.idiomatic: second, attend the Ancestral Temple in person for all four seasons;

sentences.zh: 三曰先定首相；

translations.literal: third, first fix the chief minister;
translations.idiomatic: third, appoint a chief minister first;

sentences.zh: 四曰朝見群臣，訪問時政得失；

translations.literal: fourth, hold court and see the ministers, inquiring into the gains and losses of policies of the time;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, hold court, receive ministers, and ask what policy gains or loses;

sentences.zh: 五曰詔儒臣以時侍講；

translations.literal: fifth, order Confucian officials to attend and lecture at appointed times;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, summon Confucian scholars to lecture the throne on schedule;

sentences.zh: 六曰設太學及府州儒學，教養生徒；

translations.literal: sixth, establish the Imperial Academy and prefectural and district Confucian schools to nurture students;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, found the Imperial Academy and local schools to train students;

sentences.zh: 七曰行誥命以褒善敘勞；

translations.literal: seventh, issue edicts of appointment to praise the good and record merit;
translations.idiomatic: seventh, issue edicts of reward for virtue and service;

sentences.zh: 八曰異章服以別貴賤；

translations.literal: eighth, differentiate robes and caps to distinguish noble and base;
translations.idiomatic: eighth, distinguish dress by rank;

sentences.zh: 九曰正禮儀以肅宮庭；

translations.literal: ninth, rectify ritual to solemnize the palace;
translations.idiomatic: ninth, correct ritual to dignify the court;

sentences.zh: 十曰定官制以省內外冗員；

translations.literal: tenth, fix the official system to reduce redundant posts within and without;
translations.idiomatic: tenth, reform offices to cut redundancy;

sentences.zh: 十一曰講究錢穀以裕國用；

translations.literal: eleventh, investigate money and grain to enrich state revenue;
translations.idiomatic: eleventh, study revenue to fill the treasury;

sentences.zh: 十二曰訪求曉習音律者以協太常雅樂；

translations.literal: twelfth, seek those skilled in pitch and regulation to harmonize the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' elegant music;
translations.idiomatic: twelfth, seek masters of pitch to tune the court music;

sentences.zh: 十三曰國子監不可隸集賢院，宜正其名；

translations.literal: thirteenth, the Directorate of Education must not be subordinate to the Academy of Scholarly Worthies—its name should be rectified;
translations.idiomatic: thirteenth, the Directorate of Education must not answer to the Academy of Scholarly Worthies—restore its proper status;

sentences.zh: 十四曰試補六部寺監及府州司縣吏；

translations.literal: fourteenth, test and appoint clerks of the six ministries, directorates, and prefectural, district, and county offices;
translations.idiomatic: fourteenth, examine candidates for clerks in ministries, directorates, and local offices;

sentences.zh: 十五曰增內外官吏俸祿；

translations.literal: fifteenth, increase the salaries of inner and outer officials;
translations.idiomatic: fifteenth, raise official salaries;

sentences.zh: 十六曰禁父子骨肉、奴婢相告訐者；

translations.literal: sixteenth, forbid fathers and sons, flesh and bone, and master and slave from denouncing one another;
translations.idiomatic: sixteenth, forbid kin and servants from informing on one another;

sentences.zh: 十七曰定婚姻聘財；

translations.literal: seventeenth, fix betrothal gifts for marriage;
translations.idiomatic: seventeenth, set standards for marriage gifts;

sentences.zh: 十八​​曰罷行用官錢營什一之利；

translations.literal: eighteenth, abolish using official money to pursue one-tenth profits;
translations.idiomatic: eighteenth, end investing official funds for ten-percent gain;

sentences.zh: 十九曰复笞杖以別輕重之罪；

translations.literal: nineteenth, restore the bastinado to distinguish light and heavy crimes;
translations.idiomatic: nineteenth, restore beating with the rod to mark degrees of guilt;

sentences.zh: 二十曰郡縣吏自中統前仕宦者，宜加優異；

translations.literal: twentieth, district and county clerks who served before Zhongtong should receive preferential treatment;
translations.idiomatic: twentieth, favor clerks who served before Zhongtong;

sentences.zh: 二十一曰為治之道宜各從本俗。

translations.literal: twenty-first, the Way of governing should in each case follow native custom.
translations.idiomatic: twenty-first, let each region be governed according to its own customs.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor read the memorial and approved it with praise.

sentences.zh: 未幾，升秘書少監，預修《大一統志》。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and took part in compiling the Comprehensive Gazetteer.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became vice director of the Secretariat and helped compile the Comprehensive Gazetteer.

sentences.zh: 秩滿歸兗州，以貲業悉讓弟楷，鄉里稱焉。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned to Yanzhou and gave all his property to his younger brother Kai; the village praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he went home to Yanzhou and gave his entire estate to his brother Kai; neighbors praised his generosity.

sentences.zh: 大德三年，以國子司業召，未赴，卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dade he was summoned as vice commissioner of the Directorate of Education but did not go; he died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 3 he was summoned as vice commissioner of the Directorate of Education but died before taking office, aged sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 桓為人寬厚，事親篤孝，博覽群籍，尤精篆籀之學。

translations.literal: Huan as a man was generous and mild; in serving his parents he was deeply filial; he broadly read all books and was especially expert in seal-script studies.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was generous and dutiful, a devoted son who read widely and excelled in seal script.

sentences.zh: 著《六書統》、《六書溯源》、《書學正韻》，大抵推明許慎之說，而意加深，皆行於世。

translations.literal: He authored Comprehensive Six Scripts, Origins of the Six Scripts, and Correct Rhymes of Calligraphy; in general he extended Xu Shen's doctrines with deeper intent—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Comprehensive Six Scripts, Origins of the Six Scripts, and Correct Rhymes of Calligraphy deepened Xu Shen's philology and circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 楊果，字正卿，祁州蒲陰人。

translations.literal: Yang Guo, styled Zhengqing, was a native of Puyin in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guo, courtesy name Zhengqing, came from Puyin in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼失怙恃，自宋遷亳，复徙居許昌，以章句授徒為業，流寓轗軻十餘年。

translations.literal: In youth he lost both parents; from Song he moved to Bo, then again relocated to Xuchang; he made his living teaching the classics clause by clause and wandered in hardship more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he fled Song for Bo, then Xuchang, teaching classical texts for a living through more than ten years of wandering hardship.

sentences.zh: 金正大甲申，登進士第。

translations.literal: In jiazi of the Zhengda era of Jin he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin's Zhengda jiazi year he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 會參政李蹊行大司農於許，果以詩送之，蹊大稱賞，歸言於朝，用為偃師令。

translations.literal: When Vice Administrator Li Xi toured as Grand Minister of Agriculture at Xu, Guo sent him a poem in farewell; Xi greatly praised it and, returning, spoke of him at court; he was appointed magistrate of Yanshi.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Administrator Li Xi inspected agriculture at Xu, Guo sent him a parting poem that Xi praised to the court; Guo was made magistrate of Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 到官，以廉幹稱，改蒲城，改陝，皆劇縣也。

translations.literal: On taking office he was known for integrity and efficiency; he was transferred to Pucheng, then to Shan—all difficult counties.
translations.idiomatic: In office he won praise for integrity and drive; transfers to Pucheng and then Shan—both demanding counties—followed.

sentences.zh: 果有應變材，能治煩劇，諸縣以果治效為最。

translations.literal: Guo had talent for meeting change and could govern what was vexatious and pressing; among the districts Guo's governing effect ranked highest.
translations.idiomatic: Resourceful in crisis, he mastered the hardest posts; among the counties his record stood first.

sentences.zh: 金亡，歲己丑，楊奐徵河南課稅，起果為經歷。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, in the year jichou Yang Huan was charged to levy taxes in Henan and Guo was raised as secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's fall, in jichou Yang Huan took charge of Henan taxes and Guo became his secretary.

sentences.zh: 未幾，史天澤經略河南，果為參議。

translations.literal: Before long Shi Tianze directed Henan and Guo became administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shi Tianze took charge of Henan and made Guo his aide.

sentences.zh: 時兵革之餘，法度草創，果隨宜贊畫，民賴以安。

translations.literal: At that time, in the aftermath of war, laws were newly drafted; Guo advised as circumstances required and the people relied on him for peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the wake of war, with laws still being shaped, Guo advised as need arose and the people found stability through him.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統元年，設十道宣撫使，命果為北京宣撫使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong of Shizu, ten circuit pacification commissioners were established and Guo was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Shizu's Zhongtong 1 ten circuit pacification commissioners were created; Guo became Pacification Commissioner of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed vice administrator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became vice administrator of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及例罷，猶詔與左丞姚樞等日赴省議事。

translations.literal: When the rule for dismissal applied, he was still ordered with Left Assistant Administrator Yao Shu and others to attend the Secretariat daily for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Though rotated out by rule, he was still ordered with Left Assistant Yao Shu and others to attend Secretariat deliberations daily.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，出為懷孟路總管，大修學廟。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan he went out as chief administrator of Huai-Meng Route and greatly repaired the school temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 6 he became chief administrator of Huai-Meng Route and rebuilt its school temple on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 以前嘗為中書執政官，移文申部，特不署名。

translations.literal: Because he had formerly been a Secretariat executive official, he sent a dispatch to the ministry reporting this and especially did not sign his name.
translations.idiomatic: Having once been a Secretariat executive, he notified the ministry and deliberately omitted his signature from documents.

sentences.zh: 以老致政，卒於家，年七十五，諡文獻。

translations.literal: He retired on account of age and died at home, aged seventy-five; posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He retired for age and died at home, seventy-five, posthumous name Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 果性聰敏，美風姿，工文章，尤長於樂府，外若沉默，內懷智用，善諧謔，聞者絕倒。

translations.literal: Guo's nature was keen and clever, his bearing handsome; he was skilled in literary composition and especially excelled in yuefu; outwardly he seemed silent, inwardly he harbored resourcefulness; he was good at banter and wit, and listeners were convulsed with laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and handsome, skilled in prose and especially yuefu, he seemed quiet outwardly yet was sharp within, a wit whose jests left hearers helpless with laughter.

sentences.zh: 微時，避亂河南，娶羈旅中女，後登科，歷顯仕，竟與偕老，不易其初心，人以是稱之。

translations.literal: In humble days, fleeing chaos in Henan, he married a woman met in travel; later he passed the examination, held eminent office, and to the end grew old with her without changing his first heart—men praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing chaos in Henan he married a woman he met on the road; after the jinshi and high office he kept her to the end—men praised his constancy.

sentences.zh: 有《西庵集》，行於世。

translations.literal: He had Western Hermitage Collection, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Western Hermitage Collection circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 王構，字肯堂，東平人。

translations.literal: Wang Gou, styled Kentang, was a native of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gou, courtesy name Kentang, was from Dongping.

sentences.zh: 父公淵，遭金末之亂，其兄三人挈家南奔，公淵獨誓死守墳墓，伏草莽中，諸兄呼之不出，號慟而去，卒得存其家，而三兄不知所終。

translations.literal: His father Gongyuan, encountering the chaos at the end of Jin, had three elder brothers who took their families and fled south; Gongyuan alone swore to die guarding the graves, lay hidden in the grass, and though his brothers called him he would not come out; they wailed and left, and in the end he preserved the family, while the three elder brothers were never heard of again.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gongyuan, in Jin's final chaos, saw three elder brothers flee south with their households while he alone swore to guard the tombs, hiding in the grass though they called; they wept and departed. He saved the clan; the three brothers vanished without trace.

sentences.zh: 構少穎悟，風度凝厚。

translations.literal: Gou in youth was keen and perceptive, his bearing composed and substantial.
translations.idiomatic: Gou was bright as a youth, his manner grave and steady.

sentences.zh: 學問該博，文章典雅，弱冠以詞賦中選，為東平行台掌書紀。

translations.literal: His learning was comprehensive and his literary compositions elegant; at weak cap he was selected by rhapsody and ode and became recorder of the Eastern Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and elegant in prose, he won selection by rhapsody in his youth and became recorder of the Eastern Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 參政賈居貞一見器重，俾其子受學焉。

translations.literal: Vice Administrator Jia Juzhen, on one meeting, greatly esteemed him and had his son study under him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Administrator Jia Juzhen esteemed him at first sight and sent his son to study with him.

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，授翰林國史院編修官。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan he was appointed compiler of the National History Academy in the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 11 he became compiler in the Hanlin National History Academy.

sentences.zh: 時遣丞相伯顏伐宋，先下詔讓之，命構屬草以進，世祖大悅。

translations.literal: When the court sent Chancellor Bayan to attack Song, it first issued an edict of reproach; Gou was ordered to draft it and present it; Shizu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan was sent against Song, the court first issued a denunciation; Gou drafted it to the Emperor's great satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 宋亡，構與李槃同被旨，至杭取三館圖籍、太常天章禮器儀仗，歸於京師。

translations.literal: When Song fell, Gou with Li Pan together received the order to go to Hangzhou to take the libraries of the Three Institutes, the ritual vessels and regalia of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Heavenly Manifestation, and return them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Song's fall Gou and Li Pan were ordered to Hangzhou to bring back the Three Institutes' books, the ritual vessels of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Heavenly Manifestation, and the regalia to the capital.

sentences.zh: 凡所薦拔，皆時之名士。

translations.literal: All whom he recommended and promoted were eminent men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Every man he recommended was a leading figure of the day.

sentences.zh: 十三年秋，還，入覲，遷應奉翰林文字，升修撰。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the thirteenth year he returned, entered audience, was transferred to Hanlin Academician in Attendance on the Emperor, and promoted to reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year's autumn he returned, had audience, became Hanlin Academician in Attendance, and was promoted reviser.

sentences.zh: 丞相和禮霍孫由翰林學士承旨拜司徒，辟構為司直。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Heli Huosun, from Hanlin Academician Expositor, received appointment as Grand Preceptor, he recruited Gou as Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: After Heli Huosun rose from Hanlin expositor to Grand Preceptor, he took Gou on as his registrar.

sentences.zh: 時丞相阿合馬為盜擊死，世祖亦悟其奸，復相和禮霍孫，更張庶務，構之謀畫居多。

translations.literal: At that time Chancellor Ahmad had been struck down and killed by robbers; the Founder also perceived his treachery, made Heli Huosun chancellor again, and renewed the manifold affairs of state—Gou's planning and counsel figured in most of it.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad had just been killed by assassins; Kublai, seeing his corruption at last, restored Heli Huosun and set state business on a new course—much of it shaped by Gou's advice.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部、禮部郎中，審囚河南，多所平反。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Director in the Ministries of Personnel and of Rites, tried prisoners in Henan, and reversed many wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: He held directorships in the Ministries of Personnel and Rites, reviewed cases in Henan, and overturned many unjust sentences.

sentences.zh: 改太常少卿，定親享太廟儀注。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and fixed the ritual protocols for the emperor's personal offerings at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, he codified the rites for the emperor's own sacrifices in the Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 擢淮東提刑按察副使，召見便殿，親授制書，賜上尊酒以遣之。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Commissioner of the Huaidong Surveillance Commission for Punishments; summoned to the Privy Chamber, he was personally given the imperial commission and sent off with premium wine.
translations.idiomatic: Raised to vice commissioner on the Huaidong surveillance circuit, he was called to the Privy Chamber, handed his commission by the emperor's own hand, and dismissed with fine wine.

sentences.zh: 尋以治書侍御史召。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled as Attending Censor with the Writing Brush.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was summoned back as an attending censor.

sentences.zh: 屬桑哥為相，俾與平章卜忽木檢核燕南錢穀，而督其逋負。

translations.literal: When Sangtu became chancellor, [Gou] was ordered together with Grand Councillor Buhumu to audit the revenues and grain of Yan South and to press collection of arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chancellor Sangtu he was paired with Grand Councillor Buhumu to audit Yan South revenues and grain and to chase down unpaid levies.

sentences.zh: 以十一月晦行，期歲終復命。

translations.literal: He set out on the last day of the eleventh month, with the term fixed for reporting back at year's end.
translations.idiomatic: He left on the last day of the eleventh month and was due to report back before the year was out.

sentences.zh: 明年春還，宿盧溝驛，度逾期，禍且不測，謂卜忽木曰：「設有罪，構當以身任之，不以累公也。」

translations.literal: Returning the next spring, he lodged at Lugou Post Station; realizing he had passed the deadline and calamity was unpredictable, he said to Buhumu: "If there is guilt, Gou shall bear it in his own person and not involve you."
translations.idiomatic: He came back the following spring and stopped at Lugou station. Seeing he was overdue and punishment uncertain, he told Buhumu, "If anyone must answer for this, let it be me—not you."

sentences.zh: 會桑哥死，乃免。

translations.literal: Just then Sangtu died, and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Sangtu died about that time, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 有旨出銓選江西。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him out for personnel selection in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Jiangxi on a provincial appointment commission.

sentences.zh: 入翰林，為侍講學士。

translations.literal: He entered the Hanlin Academy as Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Hanlin Academy as lecturer-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，構撰諡冊。

translations.literal: When the Founder died, Gou drafted the posthumous title document.
translations.idiomatic: At Kublai's death Gou wrote the posthumous epithet scroll.

sentences.zh: 構歷事三朝，練習臺閣典故，凡祖宗諡冊冊文皆所撰定，朝廷每有大議，必諮訪焉。

translations.literal: Gou served three reigns and was practiced in the precedents of the Secretariat and Pavilion; all posthumous titles and enshrinement texts for the forefathers were set down by him, and whenever the court had a great deliberation, counsel was sought from him.
translations.idiomatic: Gou served three emperors and knew Secretariat precedent by heart. He drafted every ancestral posthumous title and enshrinement text, and the court consulted him on every weighty question.

sentences.zh: 喜薦引寒士，前後省台、翰苑所辟，無慮數十人，後居清要，皆有名於時。

translations.literal: He delighted in recommending and advancing poor scholars; those recruited over the years by the Secretariat, the Censorate, and the Academy were not fewer than several tens, and later, holding clean, important posts, all were famous in their time.
translations.idiomatic: He loved lifting up obscure scholars. The men he helped into the Secretariat, the Censorate, and the Hanlin numbered in the dozens; each later rose to a notable post.

sentences.zh: 子士熙，仕至中書參政，卒官南台御史中丞。

translations.literal: His son Shixi rose to Associate Administrator of the Secretariat and died in office as Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Southern Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shixi reached associate administrator of the Secretariat and died in office as vice censor-in-chief on the Southern Censorate.

sentences.zh: 士點，淮西廉訪司僉事。

translations.literal: Shidian was Assistant Commissioner of the Huai West Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Shidian served as assistant commissioner on the Huai West surveillance circuit.

sentences.zh: 皆能以文學世其家。

translations.literal: All were able to hand down the family's literary tradition.
translations.idiomatic: The family kept its literary reputation through them all.

sentences.zh: ○魏初

translations.literal: ○ Wei Chu
translations.idiomatic: ○ Wei Chu

sentences.zh: 魏初，字大初，弘州順聖人。

translations.literal: Wei Chu, courtesy name Dachu, was a native of Shunsheng in Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chu, styled Dachu, came from Shunsheng in Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從祖璠，金貞佑三年進士，補尚書省令史。

translations.literal: His collateral ancestor's grandfather Fan passed the jinshi in the third year of Zhenyou of Jin and was appointed Clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Fan, a generation back, took jinshi in Jin Zhenyou 3 and became a Secretariat clerk.

sentences.zh: 金宣宗求直言，璠首論將相非人，及不當立德陵事，疏奏，不報。

translations.literal: When the Jin Xuānzong sought frank counsel, Fan was first to argue that the generals and ministers were unworthy men and that building the Virtue Tomb was improper; his memorial was submitted but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuānzong of Jin asked for blunt counsel, Fan was first to say the high command was unfit and that the Virtue Tomb should not be built. The memorial went in; nothing came back.

sentences.zh: 後復上言：「國勢危逼，四方未聞有勤王之舉，隴右地險食足，其帥完顏胡斜虎亦可委仗，宜遣人往論大計。」

translations.literal: Later he again submitted: "The state's peril presses close; nowhere in the four quarters is there word of armies coming to aid the throne. Longyou's terrain is rugged and its grain ample—its commander Wanyan Huxiehu may also be entrusted; it is fitting to send someone to discuss the great plan with him."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote again: "The realm is in grave danger, yet no loyal army marches from any quarter. Longyou is defensible and well provisioned; its commander Wanyan Huxiehu is a man you can rely on. Send an envoy and lay the great plan before him."

sentences.zh: 大臣不悅而止。

translations.literal: The great ministers were displeased and let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers took offense, and the proposal died.

sentences.zh: 閱數月，胡斜虎兵不來，已無及，金主悔焉。

translations.literal: After several months Huxiehu's troops did not come; it was already too late, and the Jin ruler regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Months passed without Huxiehu's army. By then nothing could be done, and the Jin emperor repented too late.

sentences.zh: 金將武仙軍次五垛山不進。

translations.literal: The Jin general Wu Xian's army halted at Wuduo Mountain and would not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general Wu Xian camped at Wuduo Mountain and refused to move.

sentences.zh: 求使仙者，或薦璠，即授朝列大夫、翰林修撰，給騎四人以從。

translations.literal: When an envoy to summon Xian was sought, someone recommended Fan; he was immediately appointed Grand Master of the Court and Hanlin Compiler, with four mounted attendants to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: The court needed someone to summon Wu Xian; Fan was recommended, made Grand Master of the Court and Hanlin compiler, and given four horsemen for the journey.

sentences.zh: 至則仙已遁去，部曲亦多散亡，璠撫循招集，得數千人，推其中材勇者為帥長，仍制符印予之，以矯制自劾，金主謂其處置得宜。

translations.literal: On arrival Xian had already fled; his troops too were largely scattered. Fan comforted and gathered them, obtaining several thousand men; he chose the bravest among them for squad leaders, still made tally-seals and gave them out, and on his own authority reported himself for punishment—the Jin ruler said his handling was proper.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived to find Wu Xian gone and the army in pieces. Fan rallied several thousand men, picked the bravest as squad chiefs, issued tally-seals on his own authority, and reported himself for discipline. The Jin emperor approved his handling.

sentences.zh: 繼聞仙率餘眾保留山，璠直趣仙所宣諭之。

translations.literal: Learning next that Xian was leading his remaining troops at Baoliu Mountain, Fan went straight to Xian's camp to proclaim the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Wu Xian still held the remnant of his force at Baoliu Mountain, Fan went straight to his camp to deliver the imperial command.

sentences.zh: 或讒於仙，謂璠欲奪其軍，仙怒，命士拔刃若欲鏦璠然，且引一吏與璠辨。

translations.literal: Someone slandered Fan to Xian, saying Fan meant to seize his army; Xian was enraged and ordered soldiers to bare blades as if to run Fan through, and brought out a clerk to argue with Fan.
translations.idiomatic: A whisper reached Wu Xian that Fan meant to steal his command. Enraged, Xian had blades drawn as if to kill Fan and set a petty clerk to dispute with him.

sentences.zh: 璠不為動，大言曰：「王人雖微，序於諸侯之上，將軍縱不加禮，奈何聽讒邪之言，欲以小吏置對耶！

translations.literal: Fan did not stir and spoke loudly: "Though the king's man is low in rank, he stands above the feudal lords. Even if the general withholds courtesy, how can you heed slander and set a petty clerk to bandy words with me!
translations.idiomatic: Fan never flinched. "I may be humble," he said, "but I rank above every lord. Even if you owe me no courtesy, will you heed slander and pit a clerk against the emperor's envoy?

sentences.zh: 且將軍跳山谷，而左右無異心者，以天子大臣故也，苟不知尊天子，安知麾下無如將軍者？

translations.literal: Moreover, the reason your men follow you through ravines and cliffs without wavering is that you are the Son of Heaven's minister. If you do not honor the Son of Heaven, how do you know your ranks hold no one like you?
translations.idiomatic: Your men cling to you in the hills because you serve the Son of Heaven. Dishonor the throne, and who can say your own officers will not turn on you as you have turned on me?

sentences.zh: 不然，吾有死，無辱命。」

translations.literal: If not, I have death—no disgrace to my commission."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I choose death before a failed mission."

sentences.zh: 仙不能屈。

translations.literal: Xian could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian could not break him.

sentences.zh: 璠复激使進兵，不應。

translations.literal: Fan again pressed him to advance the army; he would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Fan urged him again to march; he still refused.

sentences.zh: 比還，金主已遷歸德，复遷蔡州。

translations.literal: By the time Fan returned, the Jin ruler had already moved to Guide and then to Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan got back, the Jin court had already fled to Guide, then to Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 金亡，璠無所歸，乃北還鄉里。

translations.literal: When Jin perished Fan had nowhere to go and returned north to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Jin fell; with nowhere left to serve, Fan went home to the north.

sentences.zh: 庚戌歲，世祖居潛邸，聞璠名，徵至和林，訪以當世之務。

translations.literal: In the gengxu year, while the Founder still held his princely residence, hearing Fan's name he summoned him to Karakorum and questioned him on the affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengxu year Kublai, still heir apparent, heard of Fan and called him to Karakorum to ask his view of the times.

sentences.zh: 璠條陳便宜三十餘事，舉名士六十餘人以對，世祖嘉納，後多采用焉。

translations.literal: Fan set forth in articles more than thirty measures of practical benefit and named more than sixty eminent scholars in reply; the Founder praised and accepted them, and many were later adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Fan laid out more than thirty practical reforms and named over sixty scholars of note. Kublai welcomed the counsel and later put much of it into practice.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒於和林，年七十，賜諡靖肅。

translations.literal: He died of illness at Karakorum at age seventy; the posthumous title Jingsu was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Karakorum, aged seventy, and was given the posthumous name Jingsu.

sentences.zh: 帝宴群臣於上都行宮，有不能釂大卮者，免其冠服。

translations.literal: The Emperor feasted the ministers at the Shangdu traveling palace; those who could not drain a great goblet had their caps and robes taken away.
translations.idiomatic: At the Shangdu palace the emperor gave a feast at which any minister who could not empty a great cup was stripped of cap and robe.

sentences.zh: 初上疏曰：「臣聞君猶天也，臣猶地也，尊卑之禮，不可不肅。

translations.literal: Chu first submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that the ruler is like Heaven and the minister like earth—the ritual of high and low must not be neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chu memorialized first: "I have heard that the ruler is as Heaven and the minister as earth; the rites that separate high from low must be kept.

sentences.zh: 方今內有太常、有史官、有起居注，以議典禮、記言動；

translations.literal: Within there are the Director of Imperial Sacrifices, the Historiographer, and the Recorder of the Ruler's Actions, to deliberate ritual and record words and deeds;
translations.idiomatic: Within the court the Director of Sacrifices, the historiographers, and the recorder of the ruler's conduct deliberate ritual and set down every word and act;

sentences.zh: 外有高麗、安南使者入貢，以觀中國之儀。

translations.literal: without, envoys from Koryŏ and Annam come to offer tribute, to observe the Middle Kingdom's ceremonial bearing.
translations.idiomatic: while from without envoys of Koryŏ and Annam come bearing tribute to witness how the Middle Kingdom conducts itself.

sentences.zh: 昨聞錫宴大臣，威儀弗謹，非所以尊朝廷、正上下也。」

translations.literal: Yesterday I heard that at a feast for great ministers the majesty of deportment was not careful—this is not the way to honor the court and rectify high and low."
translations.idiomatic: Yet yesterday's feast for the great ministers showed no care for dignity or order. That is no way to honor the throne or teach respect between ruler and subject."

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝欣納之，仍諭侍臣自今毋復為此舉。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the Emperor gladly accepted it and still instructed the attendant ministers that from this time they must not again perform this act.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with pleasure and told his attendants never to hold such a feast again.

sentences.zh: 時襄樊未下，將括民為兵，或請自大興始。

translations.literal: At that time Xiangyang and Fancheng had not yet fallen; the plan was to conscript the people as soldiers, and some asked that it begin with Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang and Fancheng still held out; the court meant to press the people into service, and some proposed starting with Daxing.

sentences.zh: 初言：「京師天下之本，要在殷盛，建邦之初，詎宜騷動！」

translations.literal: Chu said: "The capital is the root of all under Heaven; what matters is that it flourish. At the founding of the realm, how can it be fitting to stir it up!"
translations.idiomatic: Chu objected: "The capital is the root of the empire; it must stay strong. In the founding of a dynasty, why disturb it first?"

sentences.zh: 遂免括大興兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon conscription in Daxing was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Daxing was spared the levy.

sentences.zh: 初又言：「舊制，常參官諸州刺史，上任三日，舉一人自代。

translations.literal: Chu also said: "By old regulation, regularly attending officials and prefects, within three days of taking office, were to nominate one man to replace themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged restoring an old rule: every regularly attending official and every prefect, within three days of appointment, should name a successor.

sentences.zh: 況風紀之職與常員異，請自監察御史、按察司官，在任一歲，各舉一人自代，所舉不當，有罰，不惟砥礪風節，亦可為國得人。」

translations.literal: How much more do posts of discipline differ from ordinary offices—your servant asks that from Supervising Censors and surveillance commissioners, after one year in post each nominate one man to replace himself; if the nomination is improper there shall be punishment. This will not only hone integrity but also obtain men for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Disciplinary posts matter even more. Let every supervising censor and surveillance commissioner, after one year, nominate his own replacement, with penalties for a poor choice. That would sharpen integrity and fill the state with able men."

sentences.zh: 遂舉勸農副使劉宣自代。

translations.literal: Thereupon he nominated Vice Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture Liu Xuan to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then nominated Liu Xuan, vice commissioner for encouraging agriculture, as his own successor.

sentences.zh: 出僉陝西四川按察司事，歷陝西河東按察副使，入為治書侍御史。

translations.literal: He went out as Assistant Commissioner of the Shaanxi and Sichuan Surveillance Commission, served as Vice Commissioner of the Shaanxi and Hedong Surveillance Commission, and entered as Attending Censor with the Writing Brush.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the Shaanxi–Sichuan surveillance circuit, then as deputy on the Shaanxi–Hedong circuit, and returned to court as attending censor.

sentences.zh: 又以侍御史行御史臺事於揚州，擢江西按察使，尋徵拜侍御史。

translations.literal: Again as Attending Censor he conducted Censorate affairs at Yangzhou; he was advanced to Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi, and soon after was summoned and appointed Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: As attending censor he ran Censorate business at Yangzhou, was promoted to Jiangxi surveillance commissioner, and was soon recalled as attending censor again.

sentences.zh: 行台移建康，出為中丞，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: When the Branch Secretariat moved to Jiankang he went out as Vice Censor-in-Chief; he died at age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: When the branch secretariat moved to Jiankang he became vice censor-in-chief and died there at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 子必復，集賢侍講學士。

translations.literal: His son Bifu was Lecturer-in-Waiting of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bifu became lecturer-in-waiting in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: ○焦養直

translations.literal: ○ Jiao Yangzhi
translations.idiomatic: ○ Jiao Yangzhi

sentences.zh: 焦養直，字無咎，東昌堂邑人。

translations.literal: Jiao Yangzhi, courtesy name Wujiu, was a native of Tangyi in Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Yangzhi, styled Wujiu, came from Tangyi in Dongchang.

sentences.zh: 夙以才器稱。

translations.literal: From early on he was famed for talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: He had been known since youth for ability and judgment.

sentences.zh: 至元十八年，世祖改符寶郎為典瑞監，思得一儒者居之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan the Founder changed the Seal-and-Tally Officer to the Directorate of Auspicious Commissions and wished to place a Confucian scholar in charge.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 18 Kublai renamed the seal-and-tally office the Directorate of Auspicious Commissions and wanted a Confucian scholar to head it.

sentences.zh: 近臣有以養直薦者，帝即命召見，敷對稱旨，以真定路儒學教授超拜典瑞少監。

translations.literal: A close attendant recommended Yangzhi; the Emperor at once ordered him summoned. His replies in audience matched the Emperor's intent, and he was promoted over the regular steps from Professor of Confucian Learning on the Zhending circuit to Vice Director of Auspicious Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: A court intimate named Yangzhi; Kublai summoned him at once. He answered so well that he skipped from Zhending professor of Confucian learning straight to vice director of the directorate.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，從征乃顏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he followed the campaign against Nayan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 he marched on the Nayan campaign.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，賜宅一區。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year a residence in one ward was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 he received a house in the capital.

sentences.zh: 入侍帷幄，陳說古先帝王政治，帝聽之，每忘倦。

translations.literal: He attended within the curtained quarters and discoursed on the governance of ancient emperors and kings; the Emperor listened and each time forgot weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He attended the emperor in private and lectured on the politics of ancient kings; Kublai listened until he forgot fatigue.

sentences.zh: 嘗語及漢高帝起自側微，誦所舊聞，養直從容論辨，帝即開納，由是不薄高帝。

translations.literal: Once the talk turned to how Emperor Gaozu of Han rose from humble station; reciting what he had long heard, Yangzhi answered with easy reasoning and debate, and the Emperor at once opened his mind to it—whereby he no longer slighted Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Once the talk turned to Gaozu of Han rising from nothing. Yangzhi answered with easy, pointed reasoning, and the emperor took it to heart—after which he stopped looking down on Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，成宗幸柳林，命養直進講《資治通鑑》，因陳規諫之言，詔賜酒及鈔萬七千五百貫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade, when Emperor Chengzong visited Willow Grove, he ordered Yangzhi to advance and lecture on the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, and because he offered words of remonstrance, an edict granted wine and seventeen thousand five hundred strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 1, when Chengzong visited Willow Grove, he had Yangzhi lecture from the Comprehensive Mirror and offer remonstrance. The emperor rewarded him with wine and 17,500 strings of paper money.

sentences.zh: 二年，賜金帶、象笏。

translations.literal: In the second year a gold belt and ivory tablet were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he received a gold belt and ivory tablet.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷集賢侍講學士，賜通犀帶。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Lecturer-in-Waiting of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and granted a rhinoceros-horn belt.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he became lecturer-in-waiting in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and was given a rhinoceros-horn belt.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔傅太子於宮中，啟沃誠至，帝聞之，大悅。

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict ordered him to tutor the Crown Prince in the palace; his earnest instruction reached the heir, and when the Emperor heard of it he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was ordered to tutor the crown prince in the palace. He instructed with such sincerity that Chengzong heard of it and was delighted.

sentences.zh: 八年，代祀南海。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he performed sacrifice at the Southern Sea in the emperor's stead.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he carried out the sacrifice to the Southern Sea on the emperor's behalf.

sentences.zh: 九年，進集賢學士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was advanced to Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he rose to academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 十一年，升太子諭德。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Preceptor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he became preceptor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，授集賢大學士，謀議大政悉與焉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida he was appointed Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and in deliberating great policy he shared in all of it.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 1 he became grand academician and was consulted on every major policy question.

sentences.zh: 告老歸而卒，贈資德大夫、河南等處行中書省右丞，諡文靖。

translations.literal: He requested retirement on grounds of age, returned home, and died; he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Cherishing Virtue and Right Vice Administrator of the Branch Secretariat for Henan and other places, with the posthumous title Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire, went home, and died. Posthumously he was made Grand Master of Cherishing Virtue and right vice administrator of the Henan branch secretariat, with the posthumous name Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 子德方，以廕為興國路總管府判官。

translations.literal: His son Defang entered office by hereditary privilege as Assistant Administrator of the Xingguo Route Prefectural government.
translations.idiomatic: His son Defang entered service by yin privilege as assistant administrator of Xingguo prefecture.

sentences.zh: ○孟攀鱗

translations.literal: ○ Meng Panlin
translations.idiomatic: ○ Meng Panlin

sentences.zh: 孟攀鱗，字駕之，雲內人。

translations.literal: Meng Panlin, courtesy name Jiazhi, was a native of Yunnei.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Panlin, styled Jiazhi, came from Yunnei.

sentences.zh: 曾祖彥甫，以明法為西北路招討司知事。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yanfu, through mastery of law, was Commissioner of the Northwest Route Pacification Office.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yanfu, an expert in law, served as commissioner of the Northwest Route pacification office.

sentences.zh: 有疑獄當死者百餘人，彥甫執不從，後三日得實，皆釋之。

translations.literal: In a doubtful case more than a hundred men were to die; Yanfu held firm and would not assent, and three days later the truth came out and all were released.
translations.idiomatic: In one doubtful case more than a hundred men faced execution. Yanfu refused to sign off; three days later the truth emerged and every man was freed.

sentences.zh: 祖鶴、父澤民，皆金進士。

translations.literal: His grandfather He and his father Zemin were both jinshi of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather He and his father Zemin had both passed the Jin jinshi.

sentences.zh: 攀鱗幼日誦萬言，能綴文，時號奇童。

translations.literal: From childhood Panlin recited ten thousand words a day and could compose literary pieces; at the time he was called a prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Panlin could recite ten thousand characters a day and write polished prose; people called him a wonder-child.

sentences.zh: 金正大七年，擢進士第，仕至朝散大夫、招討使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhengda of Jin he was selected in the jinshi examination and served to Grand Master for Court Discussion and Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He took jinshi in Jin Zhengda 7 and rose to Grand Master for Court Discussion and pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歲壬辰，汴京下，北歸居平陽。

translations.literal: In the renchen year Bianjing fell; he returned north and dwelt at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Bianjing fell in the renchen year he went north and settled at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 丙午，為陝西帥府詳議官，遂家長安。

translations.literal: In the bingwu year he was Detailed Review Officer of the Shaanxi commandery headquarters and then made his home in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingwu year he became detailed review officer on the Shaanxi military staff and made Chang'an his home.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統三年，授翰林待制、同修國史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong of the Founder he was appointed Hanlin Attendant Drafter and Associate Compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In Kublai's Zhongtong 3 he was made Hanlin attendant drafter and associate compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 至元初，召見，條陳七十事，大抵勸上以郊祀天地，祠太廟，制禮樂，建學校，行科舉，擇守令以字民，儲米粟以贍軍，省無名之賦，罷不急之役，百司庶府統於六部，紀綱制度悉由中書，是為長久之計。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhiyuan he was summoned to audience and set forth seventy items in articles, broadly urging the ruler to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the suburban altars, worship in the Grand Temple, establish ritual and music, found schools, hold the civil examinations, choose prefects and magistrates to cherish the people, store grain to provision the army, reduce taxes without name, abolish urgent corvée labor, unite the hundred offices and various agencies under the Six Ministries, and have statutes and institutions all proceed from the Secretariat—these were plans for long endurance.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhiyuan he was summoned and submitted seventy proposals: perform suburban sacrifices, worship in the Ancestral Temple, institute ritual and music, open schools, hold examinations, appoint caring magistrates, stock grain for the armies, cut nameless levies, end wasteful corvée, bring every agency under the Six Ministries, and let the Secretariat set all law and custom—a program meant to last.

sentences.zh: 世祖悉嘉納之，諮問諄諄。

translations.literal: The Founder praised and accepted them all and questioned him again and again with earnest care.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai welcomed every item and questioned him at length.

sentences.zh: 後論王百一、許仲平優劣，對曰：「百一文華之士，可置翰苑；

translations.literal: Later, discussing the relative merits of Wang Baiyi and Xu Zhongping, he replied: "Baiyi is a man of literary splendor—he may be placed in the Hanlin;
translations.idiomatic: Later, asked to compare Wang Baiyi and Xu Zhongping, he said, "Baiyi is a man of literary brilliance—fit for the Hanlin;

sentences.zh: 仲平明經傳道，可為後學矜式。」

translations.literal: Zhongping illuminates the classics and transmits the Way—he may serve as a model for later students."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongping masters the classics and carries the Way—he should be a model for later students."

sentences.zh: 帝深然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 又嘗召問宗廟、郊祀儀制，攀鱗悉據經典以對。

translations.literal: Again he was summoned and asked about ancestral temple and suburban sacrifice ritual; Panlin answered throughout on the basis of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned again on temple and suburban rites and answered entirely from the classics.

sentences.zh: 時帝將視祀，詔命攀鱗會太常議定禮儀，攀鱗夜畫郊祀及宗廟圖以進，帝皆親覽焉。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor was about to perform sacrifices in person; an edict ordered Panlin to meet with the Director of Imperial Sacrifices to fix the ritual. Panlin by night drew diagrams of the suburban sacrifice and the ancestral temple and presented them; the Emperor personally examined them all.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to sacrifice in person, Panlin was ordered to settle the rites with the Director of Sacrifices. He drew overnight diagrams of the suburban altar and the temple rites and presented them; the emperor studied each one himself.

sentences.zh: 復以病請西歸，帝令就議陝西五路四川行中書省事。

translations.literal: Again, on grounds of illness he requested to return west; the Emperor ordered him to deliberate on the affairs of the Branch Secretariat for the Five Circuits of Shaanxi and Sichuan while there.
translations.idiomatic: Ill again, he asked to go west. The emperor let him retire but ordered him to advise on the Shaanxi–Sichuan branch secretariat from home.

sentences.zh: 四年卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died at age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 4, aged sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 延祐三年，贈翰林學士承旨、資德大夫、上護軍、平原郡公，諡文定。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanyou he was posthumously granted Hanlin Academician Expositor, Grand Master of Cherishing Virtue, Senior Guardian of the Army, and Duke of Pingyuan Commandery, with the posthumous title Wending.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 3 he was posthumously made Hanlin expositor, Grand Master of Cherishing Virtue, senior guardian of the army, and Duke of Pingyuan, with the posthumous name Wending.

sentences.zh: ○尚野

translations.literal: ○ Shang Ye
translations.idiomatic: ○ Shang Ye

sentences.zh: 尚野，字文蔚，其先保定人，徙滿城。

translations.literal: Shang Ye, courtesy name Wenwei—his ancestors were men of Baoding who moved to Mancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Ye, styled Wenwei, came from a Baoding family that had moved to Mancheng.

sentences.zh: 野幼穎異，祖母劉，厚資之使就學。

translations.literal: From youth Ye was exceptionally bright; his grandmother Liu generously funded him to pursue learning.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was precocious as a boy; his grandmother Liu gave generously so he could study.

sentences.zh: 至元十八年，以處士徵為國史院編修官。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan, as a reclusive scholar he was summoned and appointed Compiler of the National History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 18, summoned as a recluse scholar, he became compiler at the National History Institute.

sentences.zh: 二十年，兼興文署丞，出為汝州判官，廉介有為，憲司屢薦之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he concurrently served as Vice Director of the Office for Promoting Literature; he went out as Assistant Administrator of Ruzhou, was upright and capable, and the surveillance commission repeatedly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he also served as vice director of the Office for Promoting Literature, then went out as assistant administrator of Ruzhou. He governed with integrity and energy, and the surveillance circuit recommended him again and again.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遷南陽縣尹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was transferred to be magistrate of Nanyang county.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed magistrate of Nanyang county.

sentences.zh: 初至官，獄訟充斥，野裁決無留滯，涉旬，遂無事。

translations.literal: When he first arrived at his post, lawsuits filled the courts; Ye adjudicated without delay or backlog, and within about ten days there were no pending cases.
translations.idiomatic: When he first took office the dockets were overflowing, yet Ye decided cases without delay; within ten days the courts were clear.

sentences.zh: 改懷孟河渠副使，會遣使問民疾苦，野建言：「水利有成法，宜隸有司，不宜復置河渠官。」

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Huai-Meng River Works. It happened that envoys were sent to inquire into the people's hardships; Ye submitted a proposal: "Waterworks have established regulations and ought to be placed under the regular offices; it is not appropriate to re-establish river-works officials."
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Commissioner of Huai-Meng River Works. Envoys had been sent to inquire into popular hardship, and Ye advised: "Water control already has fixed regulations; it should fall under the regular bureaus, not warrant a separate corps of river officials again."

sentences.zh: 事聞於朝，河渠官遂罷。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported to court, the river-works officials were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The report reached court, and the river-works posts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 大德六年，遷國子助教。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dade he was transferred to Assistant Instructor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 6 he became Assistant Instructor at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 諸生入宿衛者，歲從幸上都，丞相哈剌哈孫始命野分學於上都，以教諸生，仍鑄印給之，上都分學自野始。

translations.literal: Students who entered palace guard service each year accompanied the emperor to Shangdu; Grand Chancellor Hala Hasun first ordered Ye to establish a branch academy at Shangdu to teach the students, and had a seal cast and issued to it—the branch academy at Shangdu began with Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Students enrolled in the palace guard accompanied the court to Shangdu each year. Grand Chancellor Hala Hasun first charged Ye with opening a branch academy there to instruct them and had a seal cast for the school. The Shangdu branch academy began with Ye.

sentences.zh: 俄升國子博士，誨人先經學而後文藝，每謂諸生曰：「學未有得，徒事華藻，若持錢買水，所取有限，能自鑿井及泉而汲之，不可勝用矣。」

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted Doctor of the Imperial Academy. In instructing others he put classical learning first and literary ornament after, and often told the students: "If learning has not been attained but one merely pursues florid diction, it is like holding money to buy water—the amount obtained is limited; but if one can dig one's own well to the spring and draw from it, the supply cannot be exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted Doctor of the Academy. He taught others to master the classics before literary polish, and often told his students: "Learning not yet secured, yet fussing over ornament, is like buying water with cash—you only get so much. Dig your own well to the spring and draw from it, and you will never run dry."

sentences.zh: 時學舍未備，野密請御史臺，乞出帑藏所積，大建學舍以廣教育。

translations.literal: At that time the academy buildings were not complete; Ye secretly petitioned the Censorate, requesting that funds accumulated in the treasury be released to build academy quarters on a large scale and expand education.
translations.idiomatic: The academy buildings were still unfinished. Ye quietly petitioned the Censorate to release accumulated treasury funds and build new halls on a grand scale to broaden instruction.

sentences.zh: 仁宗在東宮，野為太子文學，多所裨益，時從賓客姚燧、諭德蕭渼入見，帝為加禮。

translations.literal: When Renzong was in the Eastern Palace, Ye served as Literary Tutor to the Crown Prince and benefited him in many ways; he often entered audience accompanied by the guest-official Yao Sui and the preceptor Xiao Mian, and the Emperor showed him additional courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: While Renzong was heir apparent, Ye served as his literary tutor and aided him greatly. He often attended audience with the guest-official Yao Sui and the preceptor Xiao Mian, and the Emperor treated him with special respect.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，除國子司業，近臣奏分國學西序為大都路學，帝已可其奏，野謂國學、府學混居，不合禮制，事遂寢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida he was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Academy. A close minister memorialized to separate the western quarter of the Imperial Academy as the Metropolitan Prefecture Academy; the Emperor had already approved the memorial, but Ye said that mixing Imperial Academy and prefectural academy in one residence did not accord with ritual propriety, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 1 he was made Vice Director of the Imperial Academy. A court favorite proposed splitting the academy's western wing off as the Metropolitan Prefecture school. The Emperor had already assented, but Ye argued that housing the national and prefectural academies together violated ritual order, and the plan was shelved.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜翰林直學士、知制誥同修國史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Direct Academician of the Hanlin, Controller of Edicts, and associate compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Direct Academician of the Hanlin, Controller of Edicts, and associate compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 詔野赴吏部，試用陰補官，野多所優假。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ye to go to the Ministry of Personnel to examine candidates for yin supplemental appointments; Ye showed much leniency in many cases.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Ye to the Ministry of Personnel to test candidates for hereditary privilege appointments, and he showed considerable leniency in many cases.

sentences.zh: 或病其太寬，野曰：「今初設此法，冀將來者習詩書、知禮義耳，非必責效目前也。」

translations.literal: Some criticized him as too lenient; Ye said: "This law has only just been established, in hope that those to come will study poetry and books and understand ritual and righteousness—it is not necessarily to demand results at once."
translations.idiomatic: Some faulted him for being too indulgent. Ye replied: "The rule has only just been introduced. The aim is that future appointees will study the classics and learn ritual and righteousness—not that we must demand immediate results."

sentences.zh: 眾乃服。

translations.literal: Then all submitted to his view.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues were persuaded.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，升翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was promoted Academician Lecturer-in-Attendance of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangqing 1 he was promoted Hanlin Academician Lecturer-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，改集賢侍講學士，兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he was transferred to Academician Lecturer-in-Attendance of the Jixian Hall and concurrently made Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 1 he became Lecturer-in-Attendance of the Jixian Hall and concurrently Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 二年夏，移疾歸滿城，四方來學者益眾。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year he pleaded illness and returned to Mancheng; scholars who came from all quarters to study grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year he pleaded illness and went home to Mancheng, where students from all directions gathered in ever greater numbers.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒於家，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died at home, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in the sixth year, at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 贈通奉大夫、太常禮儀院使、護軍，追封上黨郡公，諡文懿。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Grand Master for Thorough Service of Attendance, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Rites, and Defender of the Army; was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Shangdang Commandery, and given the posthumous title Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Master for Thorough Service of Attendance, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Rites, and Defender of the Army; enfeoffed as Duke of Shangdang and given the posthumous name Wenyi (Cultivated and Virtuous).

sentences.zh: 野性開敏，志趣正大，事繼母以孝聞，文辭典雅，一本於理。

translations.literal: Ye was open and quick by nature, his aspirations upright and great; he was known for filial service to his stepmother, his literary style elegant, all rooted in principle.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Ye was quick and open-minded, his aims broad and upright. He was famed for filial devotion to his stepmother, and his prose was elegant, grounded throughout in principle.

sentences.zh: 子師易，蘄州路總管府判官。

translations.literal: His son Shiyi was judicial administrator of the Qizhou Circuit Headquarters and Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiyi served as judicial administrator of the Qizhou circuit headquarters.

sentences.zh: 師簡，中奉大夫、奎章閣侍書學士、同知經筵事。

translations.literal: Shijian was Grand Master for Sagely Administration, Academician in Attendance on Calligraphy in the Kuizhang Pavilion, and Associate Director of the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: Shijian held the rank of Grand Master for Sagely Administration and served as Academician in Attendance on Calligraphy in the Kuizhang Pavilion and Associate Director of the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: ○李之紹

translations.literal: Li Zhishao
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhishao

sentences.zh: 李之紹，字伯宗，東平平陰人。

translations.literal: Li Zhishao, styled Bozong, was a native of Pingyin in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhishao, courtesy name Bozong, came from Pingyin in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 自幼穎悟聰敏，從東平李謙學。

translations.literal: From youth he was keen and intelligent; he studied under Li Qian of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was bright and quick-witted, and studied under Li Qian of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 家貧，教授鄉里，學者咸集。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he taught in his native district, and scholars all gathered.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor, so he taught in his home district, and students flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 至元三十一年，纂修《世祖實錄》，徵名儒充史職，以馬紹、李謙薦，授將仕佐郎、翰林國史院編修官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Zhiyuan, when the Veritable Records of Shizu were being compiled, eminent Confucians were summoned to serve in historiography; on recommendation of Ma Shao and Li Qian, he was appointed Assistant Gentleman for Merit and compiler of the National History Academy in the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 31, while the Veritable Records of Kublai were being compiled, eminent scholars were summoned for historiographic duty. On the recommendation of Ma Shao and Li Qian he was appointed Assistant Gentleman for Merit and compiler in the Hanlin National History Academy.

sentences.zh: 直學士姚燧欲試其才，凡翰林應酬之文，積十餘事，並以付之。

translations.literal: Direct Academician Yao Sui wished to test his talent; all the social correspondence texts of the Hanlin, more than ten items accumulated, were entrusted to him together.
translations.idiomatic: Direct Academician Yao Sui wished to test his ability and handed him more than ten pieces of routine Hanlin correspondence that had piled up.

sentences.zh: 之紹援筆立成，並以稿進。

translations.literal: Zhishao took up the brush and finished them at once, presenting all the drafts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishao took up his brush and finished them on the spot, submitting every draft.

sentences.zh: 燧驚喜曰：「可謂名下無虛士也。」

translations.literal: Sui exclaimed in delight: "Truly there are no unworthy men under a famous name."
translations.idiomatic: Sui exclaimed in delight: "A famous teacher indeed leaves no unworthy pupil."

sentences.zh: 大德二年，聞祖母疾，辭歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade, hearing that his grandmother was ill, he resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 2, on hearing that his grandmother was ill, he resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 复除編修官，升將仕郎。

translations.literal: He was again appointed compiler and promoted to Gentleman for Merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed compiler and raised to Gentleman for Merit.

sentences.zh: 六年，升應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Hanlin Academician in Attendance on the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to Hanlin Academician in Attendance.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 九年，丁母憂，累起復，終不能奪。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he entered mourning for his mother; repeatedly summoned back to office, they could not overcome his resolve in the end.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he entered mourning for his mother. Though repeatedly recalled to office, nothing could shake his resolve.

sentences.zh: 至大三年，仍授太常博士，升承事郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhida he was again appointed Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and promoted to Gentleman for Supporting Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 3 he was again made Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and promoted to Gentleman for Supporting Affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年，升承直郎、翰林待制。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Gentleman for Direct Support and Hanlin Academician in Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he rose to Gentleman for Direct Support and Hanlin Academician in Attendance.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，遷國子司業。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangqing 1 he became Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 延祐三年，升奉政大夫、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanyou he was promoted to Grand Master for Administrative Governance and Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 3 he was promoted to Grand Master for Administrative Governance and Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 夙夜孳孳，惟以教育人材為心。

translations.literal: Day and night he labored tirelessly, with nothing in mind but the education of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night he toiled, with no thought but the cultivation of talent.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月，升朝列大夫、同僉太常禮儀院事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year he was promoted to Grand Master of the Court Assembly and Associate Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Rites.
translations.idiomatic: That December of the fourth year he was made Grand Master of the Court Assembly and Associate Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Rites.

sentences.zh: 六年，改翰林直學士，復以疾還。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Direct Academician of the Hanlin and again returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Direct Academician of the Hanlin but again went home on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 七年，召為翰林直學士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned as Direct Academician of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was recalled as Direct Academician of the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，升翰林侍講學士、知制誥同修國史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi he was promoted to Academician Lecturer-in-Attendance of the Hanlin, Controller of Edicts, and associate compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizhi 2 he was promoted Hanlin Academician Lecturer-in-Attendance, Controller of Edicts, and associate compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 三年，告老而歸。

translations.literal: In the third year he requested retirement on grounds of age and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he petitioned to retire on grounds of age and returned home.

sentences.zh: 泰定三年八月卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Taiding he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of Taiding 3, aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 子勗，廕父職，同知諸暨州事。

translations.literal: His son Xu inherited his father's office and served as Associate Administrator of Zhuji Prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu inherited his father's rank and served as Associate Administrator of Zhuji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 之紹平日自以其性遇事優游少斷，故號果齊以自勵。

translations.literal: Zhishao normally considered his nature such that in affairs he was easygoing and lacking in decisiveness, so he styled himself Guoqi to encourage himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishao felt that by nature he was too easygoing and indecisive in affairs, and so took the style Guoqi to spur himself on.

sentences.zh: 有文集藏於家。

translations.literal: He had a collected works preserved at home.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings were preserved in the family.
